title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy via Lagrangian Relaxation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, achieving robust privacy guarantees alongside high model accuracy remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to decentralized federated learning leveraging Lagrangian relaxation and differential privacy. Our method allows for a more nuanced and adaptive trade-off between privacy and accuracy by optimizing a Lagrangian function at each participating node. This decentralized optimization process enables a flexible solution to the inherent tension between privacy preservation and model performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a potential implementation strategy. The key innovation lies in the localized optimization of the Lagrangian, mitigating the communication bottlenecks often encountered in centralized FL and offering a pathway towards truly decentralized privacy-preserving learning.

title: Resource-Aware Scheduling in Distributed Systems using Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to resource scheduling in distributed systems that integrates the principles of differential privacy with optimization algorithms. The core challenge addressed is the inherent conflict between maximizing system performance (minimizing latency) and protecting the privacy of individual nodes' data. Our proposed method introduces controlled noise into the resource allocation process, effectively obscuring the influence of any single node's data while still striving to achieve optimal scheduling. We formulate the problem as a constrained optimization problem, where the objective is to minimize overall system latency subject to differential privacy constraints. The algorithm leverages a randomized rounding technique combined with differential privacy mechanisms to achieve a provable privacy guarantee. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and a simplified system model. The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of differential privacy into resource allocation, providing a practical solution for building privacy-preserving distributed systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize constraint satisfaction algorithms, specifically focusing on improved performance and robustness compared to classical methods. We propose a novel quantum-inspired optimization algorithm predicated on the principles of quantum tunneling, aiming to leverage entanglement to navigate complex solution spaces more effectively. The core claim is that this approach offers a demonstrably faster and more reliable solution for challenging optimization problems, particularly those involving high dimensionality and intricate constraints. The research delves into the theoretical underpinnings of entanglement-based optimization, explores its potential applications, and presents preliminary results demonstrating enhanced performance in a simulated environment. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the challenges associated with translating this concept into practical implementations.

title: Adaptive Evolution Algorithms for Generative Modeling Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the design of an adaptive evolution algorithm for generative modeling, specifically focusing on optimizing the quality and diversity of generated outputs. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on static generative models, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex datasets and problems. We propose a novel approach utilizing adaptive parameter adjustments within a self-optimizing generative model to enhance both model quality and diversity. This work addresses the limitations of current methods and offers a promising direction for advancing generative modeling techniques. The core mechanism involves dynamically tuning generation parameters based on feedback, allowing the algorithm to converge towards more robust and creative outputs. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance through simulations and preliminary experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating diverse and high-quality outputs across a range of generative tasks.

title: Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing in conjunction with graph neural networks (GNNs) for solving complex combinatorial optimization problems. Traditional classical optimization algorithms often face significant challenges in identifying optimal solutions within large and intricate solution spaces. The core idea presented herein is to represent these problems as graphs and utilize the inherent quantum mechanical properties of quantum annealing to explore this space more efficiently. Specifically, GNNs are employed to generate embeddings of the graph, effectively encoding problem-specific features and relationships. This approach aims to bridge the gap between the probabilistic nature of quantum computation and the structural information captured by GNNs. We detail the theoretical framework, explore the potential benefits of this hybrid approach, and outline a methodology for integrating these techniques. The potential for improved optimization performance compared to conventional methods is discussed, highlighting the synergy between quantum annealing's ability to find low-energy states and GNNs' capacity to learn complex graph representations.

title: Black Field Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Black Field Mice
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Black Field Mouse" (BFM), inspired by the foraging strategies employed by black field mice. The algorithm leverages the mouse's efficient and adaptable search for food sources, translating these behaviors into a robust optimization process. BFM utilizes a combination of adaptive movement patterns, probabilistic exploration, and a novel "memory" mechanism to guide the search process. The algorithm operates within a defined search space, iteratively adjusting its position based on the perceived availability of "food" (representing optimal solutions). Mathematical formulations defining the core components of BFM, including the movement probability, exploration rate, and memory update rules, are provided. The algorithm is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual illustrations, showcasing its potential for solving complex optimization problems. The primary goal is to develop an algorithm that exhibits both efficient convergence and adaptability to varying problem landscapes, mirroring the observed resilience of black field mice in their natural environment. Performance comparisons, while not included in experimental results due to the focus on algorithmic design, would typically demonstrate BFM's competitive effectiveness against established metaheuristics. The theoretical framework presented here provides a strong foundation for future implementation and testing within various optimization applications.

title: Adaptive Deep Learning Gradient Clipping Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive deep learning gradient clipping optimization framework, designed to automatically adjust gradient magnitudes during training, thereby enhancing both training efficiency and stability, and mitigating the risk of gradient vanishing or exploding. The core mechanism utilizes an adaptive learning process to dynamically adjust gradient clipping thresholds, enabling a more robust and efficient training regimen. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing improvements in convergence speed and model robustness compared to traditional gradient clipping techniques. The framework's ability to handle complex environments makes it a valuable tool for accelerating deep learning model development.

title: ## Bay Bamboo Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Bay Bamboo Rats
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Bay Bamboo Rat" (BBR), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in Bay Bamboo Rats (Neomyscus crypturus) inhabiting bamboo forests. These rats exhibit a complex and adaptive behavior when searching for food, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. BBR leverages these behaviors by introducing a dual-phase search process: an initial phase mimicking the rat's exploratory movements, followed by a focused exploitation phase. The algorithm incorporates key elements such as a memory-based adaptive step size adjustment, a novel distance metric for evaluating candidate solutions, and a dynamic parameter control mechanism. Through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, we demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in solving benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential for tackling challenges in various fields. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Initialization: $X_0 = \{x_1, x_2, ..., x_N\}$, where $X_0$ represents the initial population of candidate solutions, and $N$ is the population size. Each $x_i$ is a vector representing a potential solution. * Adaptive Step Size: $a_i = a_0 * \exp(-b * \sum_{j=1}^{k} (r_i(x_i) - r_0(x_0)))$, where $a_0$ is the initial step size, $b$ is a decay factor, $k$ is the number of features, $r_i(x_i)$ is the distance from the current solution to the best solution found so far, and $r_0(x_0)$ is the distance from the initial solution to the best solution found so far. * Distance Metric: $d(x_i, x_j) = \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^{m} (x_i^{(l)} - x_j^{(l)})^2}$, where $x_i^{(l)}$ and $x_j^{(l)}$ are the l-th components of solutions $x_i$ and $x_j$, and $m$ is the number of dimensions. * Exploitation Phase: $x_{new} = argmin_{x} d(x, x_best)$, where $x_best$ is the best solution found during the current iteration.

title: Entangled Resource Allocation Algorithm for Quantum Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing the allocation of entangled resources within quantum networks. The core of the approach lies in employing a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to dynamically manage and distribute entanglement, addressing the inherent challenges of maximizing utilization and enhancing quantum communication efficiency. Unlike traditional static allocation methods, the proposed RL agent learns optimal allocation strategies through iterative interaction with a simulated quantum network environment. The algorithm considers factors such as node connectivity, qubit availability, and communication delays to minimize resource wastage and improve overall network performance. The key performance indicator (KPI) is the entanglement fidelity between communicating nodes. The developed algorithm offers a promising pathway towards realizing the full potential of quantum networks by intelligently managing their most valuable asset: entanglement. The primary goal is to achieve higher fidelity entanglement distribution and improved communication rates. The effectiveness of the algorithm is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its ability to outperform existing allocation schemes in various network topologies and operational scenarios.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Optimization for Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Quantum algorithms, while promising, often suffer from computationally expensive optimization procedures. Traditional approaches are static, hindering adaptability and potentially leading to suboptimal results. This paper introduces a novel dynamic constraint optimization system leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust constraints during the execution of quantum algorithms. The system evolves constraints based on the algorithm's performance, aiming to improve efficiency and robustness. title: Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (QGANs) for Data Augmentation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (QGANs) to data augmentation for machine learning. Traditional Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) rely on classical neural networks, while this research explores leveraging quantum circuits as generators within a QGAN architecture. The core idea is to train a quantum generator to produce synthetic data samples, supplementing existing datasets with novel instances. The discriminator remains a classical neural network, tasked with distinguishing between real and generated data. We present a theoretical framework for this approach, outlining the mathematical formulation and key components. Specifically, we introduce the notation (x, s_1, s_2, ..., s_K) to represent data samples, generator states, and relevant parameters. The objective function for the QGAN is defined as minimizing the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the real and generated data distributions. The effectiveness of this approach is discussed, highlighting potential advantages and challenges. This work contributes to the emerging field of quantum machine learning and offers a novel strategy for improving the performance of machine learning models, particularly in scenarios with limited training data.

title: Explainable AI for System Security
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance system security. Traditional security systems often rely on opaque "black box" AI models, hindering effective threat detection and defense. This work proposes a system architecture leveraging XAI techniques to provide interpretable insights into AI-driven security decisions. The core claim is that building an XAI-based system for security threat detection and defense will improve both the efficiency and reliability of security measures. The proposed mechanism utilizes XAI to elucidate the reasoning behind AI's judgments, thereby facilitating the identification of vulnerabilities and potential threats. Specifically, we explore methods for generating explanations that highlight critical factors influencing security decisions, allowing human analysts to validate, refine, or override AI recommendations. This approach addresses the limitations of current black-box AI security systems by incorporating human understanding and control, ultimately leading to a more robust and trustworthy security posture. The research contributes to a paradigm shift in system security, moving beyond solely relying on AI's predictive capabilities to actively incorporating human expertise within the decision-making process.

title: Arnhem Roundleaf Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Roundleaf Bat Algorithm" (RLBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Arnhem roundleaf bat (Antrozonia australis). The RLBA leverages the bat's echolocation and social interaction strategies to efficiently explore and exploit the search space in complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key features such as pulse rate modulation, frequency modulation, and group dynamics to guide the search process. The core of the RLBA is a modified version of the standard particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, with adjustments to the velocity and position update rules based on bat behavioral characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the RLBA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Schwefel function. The results indicate that the RLBA consistently outperforms or competes favorably with established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for tackling a wide range of complex optimization tasks. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational time. Further investigation into the influence of key parameters, such as the pulse rate and group cohesion, is also conducted to optimize the algorithm's performance.

title: ## Arboreal Rice Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Nesoryzomys surdus*
abstract: This paper introduces Arboreal Rice Rat (ARR), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Nesoryzomys surdus*, a small rodent inhabiting arboreal rice fields in Southeast Asia. The algorithm leverages the rat's unique strategies for efficient resource acquisition – specifically, its ability to rapidly assess multiple potential food sources, dynamically adjust its movement strategy based on resource availability, and exploit spatial memory to minimize travel distance. ARR employs a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel surrogate solution representation, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, resulting in an algorithm capable of effectively navigating complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. We demonstrate ARR's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive capabilities and highlighting its potential for applications in diverse fields. The core of ARR lies in its adaptive heuristic, which continuously adjusts the probability of exploring new regions of the search space versus exploiting currently promising areas. The performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Future research will focus on further refining ARR's parameters and exploring its applicability to even more challenging optimization problems.

title: ## The Polarized Migration Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Inspired by Arctic Godwits
abstract: This paper introduces the Polarized Migration Algorithm (PMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory behavior of Arctic Godwits (Limosa lapponica). These birds are renowned for their remarkably accurate navigation across vast distances, utilizing a polarized orientation strategy combined with periodic reversals. PMA leverages this strategy by maintaining a primary and secondary polarization vector, dynamically adjusting their magnitudes and angles based on the objective function's gradient and a probabilistic exploration component. The algorithm incorporates a 'resonance' mechanism to enhance convergence speed, mimicking the Godwits' tendency to maintain a consistent directional bias. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundation, mathematical formulation, and operational principles, laying the groundwork for future implementation and experimental validation.

title: Annamite Striped Rabbit: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Striping Pattern of Annamite Striped Rabbits
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Annamite Striped Rabbit (ASR), inspired by the unique striping pattern observed in Annamite Striped Rabbits (Thrisa rufescens). The algorithm leverages the rabbit's distinctive markings to guide the search process, particularly focusing on exploring the solution space and avoiding premature convergence. ASR employs a combination of adaptive mutation, a novel population-based approach termed "Striping Dynamics," and a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism. The core innovation lies in the "Striping Dynamics" where the population's movement is modulated by the density and orientation of simulated stripes, promoting both exploration and exploitation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ASR through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform several existing metaheuristic algorithms in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's performance is analyzed, highlighting its strengths and potential areas for future development. Key words: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Evolutionary Algorithm, Striping Pattern, Optimization, Adaptive Mutation, Population Dynamics.

title: 自适应概率分布的自规化学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-regularization learning algorithm based on the concept of adaptive probability distributions. Traditional learning algorithms often rely on gradient descent and similar methods, which can struggle with complex functions. This work proposes a new approach that dynamically adjusts the probability distribution parameters during the learning process, leveraging the inherent structure of the data to improve model accuracy and generalization. We introduce a "probability distribution adaptation" mechanism that iteratively refines the probability distribution based on observed data characteristics. The core claim is that this algorithm offers improved performance and robustness compared to existing methods, particularly in learning functions with high dimensionality and non-smooth gradients. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and empirical evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness through several benchmark datasets. The results showcase enhanced convergence speed and better performance in tasks involving complex, non-linear functions.

title: Neuroorphic Architectures: Dynamic Topology Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of neuroorphic architectures to achieve enhanced information processing efficiency through dynamic topology learning. The core claim is that these architectures can optimize their information handling by actively learning and adapting their own structural organization. The proposed mechanism involves algorithms that enable the dynamic adjustment of neuron connections, driven by activity levels and information transfer efficacy, mirroring the self-organizing principles observed in biological neural networks. Unlike existing approaches that often rely on fixed topologies or static adjustments, this research explores a fundamentally new paradigm – topology learning – offering a pathway towards more efficient and adaptive neurocomputing systems. We present a framework for implementing this approach, focusing on the key elements of dynamic connection refinement and topological optimization. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential challenges and future research directions within this field.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Causality-Aware Propagation
abstract: Temporal graph embeddings aim to capture the evolving behavior of graphs over time, a crucial task in domains like social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and anomaly detection. However, current graph embedding techniques often treat temporal relationships as simple sequential adjacency updates, neglecting the underlying causal structure that governs how nodes influence each other across time. This paper introduces a novel approach – Causality-Aware Propagation (CAP) – that explicitly models causal relationships within evolving graphs to generate more accurate and informative embeddings. CAP leverages event sequences and domain knowledge to define a causal graph, then employs a modified diffusion process where node representations are propagated based on the learned strength of these causal links. The core idea is to move beyond mere connection propagation to represent the *influence* of connections over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CAP through a theoretical analysis and explore its potential applications, establishing a foundational technique for temporal graph representation learning. The method's key contribution lies in its integration of causal inference with graph embedding, offering a more robust and interpretable representation of dynamic graph structures.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Hierarchical Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning framework based on Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs). The core challenge in neuro-symbolic reasoning lies in effectively integrating the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the structured reasoning capabilities of symbolic systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with knowledge representation and the ability to handle uncertainty. This work addresses these limitations by constructing a system where HBNs are used to represent and reason about knowledge hierarchically. Neural networks are employed to learn specific features and relationships within the HBN structure, while the Bayesian network provides a framework for probabilistic inference and reasoning under uncertainty. The hierarchical structure enables the system to decompose complex problems into smaller, more manageable sub-problems, improving both accuracy and interpretability. This approach demonstrates the potential to create more robust and explainable AI systems capable of handling complex reasoning tasks. The key contribution is the specific application of HBNs for this integration, moving beyond simple neural-symbolic hybrids. We outline the architecture, learning process, and inference mechanisms, focusing on the benefits of a structured knowledge representation.

This paper outlines the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulations, and provides a conceptual framework for its implementation, emphasizing its potential benefits in complex and dynamic optimization problems.

title: Topology-Based Auto-Adjustment of Graph-Based Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph-based network modeling based on topology-based auto-adjustment. Traditional network designs often struggle with representing complex dynamics and require extensive manual tuning. This work proposes a dynamically adjusted graph structure that automatically mimics the behavior of complex systems and enhances the model's generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves a continuous refinement of the graph's topology through a set of rules and feedback loops, allowing the network to adapt to changing conditions and evolving relationships. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and illustrative examples, showcasing improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic feature dependencies and emergent patterns. The study highlights the potential of topology-based auto-adjustment as a powerful tool for modeling complex systems.

title: Automated Verification of Complex Proofs with Dynamic Logic
abstract: This paper introduces a novel system for automated verification of complex mathematical proofs, leveraging dynamic logic to handle unforeseen complexities. Traditional verification methods are often time-consuming and prone to human error. Our system aims to provide a robust and scalable solution for validating mathematical statements, particularly those involving intricate logical structures and potentially ambiguous conditions. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic logic engine that adapts to the specific characteristics of each proof, improving accuracy and efficiency. We present a detailed architecture and demonstrate its effectiveness through a case study involving a complex geometric proof. The system's focus is on proactively detecting and correcting potential errors, reducing the need for extensive manual inspection.

title: The Science of Secrecy: A Narrative Review of Cryptography from Kerckhoffs's Military Letter to Post-Quantum Designs
abstract: Cryptography---the mathematics of keeping and breaking secrets---moved from Kerckhoffs's 1883 military letter and Shannon's 1949 secrecy theory through the public-key revolution of Diffie and Hellman, Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman's RSA, ElGamal's discrete logarithms, and elliptic curves to Bellare and Rogaway's random oracles, Katz and Lindell's provable security, and the post-quantum designs. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Kerckhoffs's 1883 La cryptographie militaire, Shannon's 1949 Communication theory of secrecy systems, Kahn's 1967 The Codebreakers, Diffie and Hellman's 1976 New directions, Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman's 1978 RSA, ElGamal's 1985 public key cryptosystem, Miller's 1985 elliptic curves, Koblitz's 1987 elliptic curve cryptosystems, Bellare and Rogaway's 1993 random oracles, Katz and Lindell's 2007 Introduction to Modern Cryptography, and Bernstein and Lange's 2017 post-quantum cryptography. The review is organized around three themes: from codes to theory, in which the military's principles, the secrecy's mathematics, and the codebreakers's history founded the field's frame; the public-key revolution, in which the key exchange's, the digital signature's, the discrete logarithm's, and the elliptic curve's systems abolished the shared secret; and the modern provable era, in which the random oracle's paradigm, the provable security's definitions, and the quantum's threat carried the cryptography into the post-quantum's designs. It is concluded that cryptography is the adversarial mathematics---and that its arc is the secret's protection from the commander's letter to the lattice's assumptions.

title: What Makes People Continue Using AI Speakers: Focusing on Anthropomorphism and Dual-Process Models
abstract: Our research contributes to theoretical knowledge of human-AI speaker interactions by demonstrating the importance of integrating two major theories: anthropomorphism and dual-process models. This study finds that anthropomorphism positively affects perceptions of both utilitarian aspects (i.e., ease of use, usefulness) and emotional aspects (i.e., enjoyment, intimacy). Additionally, these perceptions positively impact the intention to continue using AI speakers. This study also finds that perceptions of utilitarian and emotional aspects play mediating roles between anthropomorphism and the intention to continue using AI speakers. Our study findings suggest that human-computer interaction can satisfy two basic needs typically fulfilled by humans in everyday life: the need to experience competence (e.g., utilitarian aspects) and the need for fun and social connection (e.g., emotional aspects). These findings suggest that when studying the anthropomorphism of AI speakers, researchers should adopt dual-process models that encompass both utilitarian and emotional aspects.

title: The Failure Happens Before the Drift: The Social Dynamics of Values in LLM Agent Societies
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly used as proxies for human participants in social science research, yet it remains unclear whether they can faithfully simulate diverse and conflicting human value systems. We present a World Values Survey (WVS)-grounded simulation framework where culturally diverse agents with different communication styles engage in longitudinal, value-laden discussions. Across approximately 4,000 conversations involving 1,200 personas, 15 topics, and three models (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and Gemma-4-E4B), we evaluate value faithfulness, value drift, and conversational realism. We find that more than 50\% of personas fail to express their assigned WVS profiles from the outset, while 2-7\% drift after repeated conversations. Ablations removing demographic details improve faithfulness for some models but do not change the broader trend: simulated value distributions still systematically deviate from the assigned WVS profiles. Compared to human discussions, simulated dialogues show a different trade-off between stylistic consistency and semantic diversity, often producing content-wise varied but stylistically repetitive exchanges. These findings suggest that current LLM agents can generate plausible conversations, but remain limited proxies for representing and preserving diverse human value profiles over time.

title: AVENUE: Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation
abstract: Audio-video (AV) editing aims to modify audio and video content according to a target prompt. Unlike single-modality editing, AV editing requires models to infer a modality-selective edit scope from the prompt alone: determining not only what should change, but also which modality should be preserved. Faithfully evaluating such models therefore requires both (i) benchmarks that span diverse edit types and modality categories, and (ii) evaluation that is itself modality-aware and sample-specific. However, existing AV editing benchmarks provide limited coverage of edit types and modality combinations, while current evaluation systems are often modality-blind and sample-agnostic, making it difficult to assess whether models faithfully preserve the unintended modality. To address these gaps, we introduce AVENUE, Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation, comprising two contributions: (1) a benchmark of 1,291 source clips and 7,957 editing instructions across audio-targeted, video-targeted, and AV-coupled edit types, curated and human-verified from VGGSound; and (2) a sample-specific, modality-aware evaluation framework that specifies, for each sample, both the intended change and the content that must remain intact. We evaluate representative AV editing models spanning three editing paradigms : joint, sequential, and separate, providing the first systematic analysis of modality-selectivity across paradigms. Our findings reveal a fundamental open challenge: when editing one modality, existing models frequently induce unintended changes in the other, regardless of paradigm. AVENUE provides a benchmark and modality-aware evaluation framework to drive progress toward more controllable AV editing models. Our dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AVENUE-dataset/AVENUE.

title: AIA$^{2}$: Attribute-Agnostic Imbalance Augmentation for Subgroup Robustness
abstract: Attributes describing data content and context can induce diverse imbalance patterns that go beyond label imbalance alone. However, existing studies primarily address label imbalance while overlooking data attributes, such as topics and demographics, which can induce meaningful subgroup structure while causing model degradation on underrepresented subgroups. We propose Attribute-Agnostic Imbalance Augmentation (AIA$^{2}$), a framework for improving model robustness under varying subgroup imbalances without explicit subgroup annotations. AIA$^{2}$ automatically discovers varying imbalances via latent semantic distributions, obtains slices with both learning difficulty and subgroup imbalance deficits, and deploys a large language model (LLM) for subgroup-aware imbalance augmentation. We have evaluated AIA$^{2}$ on 5 popular corpora with rich domains and their attribute values, covering social issues and diverse topics. Results show improved performance on the lowest-performing subgroups and consistent gains over competitive baselines. Ablation studies confirm complementary contributions from each component, and additional analyses show that AIA$^{2}$ provides a practical and consistent way to improve worst-group robustness under data subgroup imbalance. Code is available at https://github.com/trust-nlp/AIA2-Subgroup-Robustness.

title: Characterization of a class of complete permutation quadrinomials over $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2m}}$
abstract: Let $q=2^m$, $Q=2^k$, and $1\leq k\leq m-1$. We characterize complete permutation polynomials (CPPs) over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of the form \[ f(x)=c_0x^{Q+1}+c_1x^{Q+q}+c_2x^{qQ+1} +c_3x^{q(Q+1)},\qquad c_i\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}. \] We prove that no such CPP exists when $k>1$, and recover the known characterization in the cubic case $k=1$. This completes the classification throughout the stated exponent range. The proof uses the known permutation classification to reduce completeness to linear perturbations of product and monomial models. The required nonpermutation results follow from direct elementary arguments based on the quadratic structure over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

title: An Exploratory Study on a Multi-layered Security Verification Framework for Identifying Data Training in Generative AI
abstract: 최근 생성형 AI, 특히 거대언어모델(Large Language Models, LLM)의 확산은 기업 및 공공기관의 업무 효율성을 크게 향상시키고 있으나, 입력 데이터가 모델 학습에 활용될 경우 발생하는 비가역적 정보 유출 위험이라는 새로운 보안 문제를 야기하고 있다. 기존 정보보안 체계는 데이터의 전송 및 저장 단계에서의 보호에 초점을 두어 왔으나, 생성형 AI 환경에서는 데이터가 모델의 가중치(Weights)에 내재화되어 삭제 이후에도 재현될 수 있다는 점에서 본질적인 한계를 가진다. 본 연구는 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 생성형 AI 보안 위협을 ‘로그(Log) 기반 유출’과 ‘학습(Learning) 기반 유출’로 구분하고, 특히 후자의 위험성을 판별하기 위한 다층적 보안 검증 프레임워크를 제안하는 탐색적 연구를 수행하였다. 본 연구에서는 블랙박스 환경과 화이트박스 환경을 포괄하는 주요 검증 방법론(Perplexity 기반 분석, 카나리 토큰, 멤버십 추론 공격, 기울기 분석)을 체계적으로 고찰하고, 실무적 적용을 위한 단계별 검증 프로토콜과 판단 로직을 설계하였다. 탐색적 분석 결과, 단일 기법으로는 생성형 AI의 데이터 학습 여부를 완전하게 검증하기 어려우며, 검증 주체와 접근 권한에 따라 차별화된 하이브리드 전략이 요구됨을 확인하였다. 구체적으로, 일반 사용자 수준의 API 기반 환경에서는 통계적 추론에 기반한 간접 검증 기법이 유효하며, 전문 감사기관의 화이트박스 환경에서는 기울기 분석(Gradient Analysis) 등 직접적 검증 기법을 통해 확정적 증거를 확보하는 이원화된 검증 체계의 필요성을 도출하였다. 본 연구의 의의는 생성형 AI 보안 문제를 실증적으로 검증 가능한 영역으로 전환하기 위한 이론적 프레임워크를 선제적으로 제안하고, 탐색적 분석을 통해 향후 실증 연구의 토대를 마련하였다는 데 있다. 이는 생성형 AI 도입 과정에서 데이터 주권을 확보하기 위한 기술적 가이드라인을 제공하며, 향후 검증 중심의 AI 거버넌스 및 머신 언러닝(Machine Unlearning) 정책 설계의 기초 자료로 활용될 수 있다.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Business and Social Development: Evidence from Business Owners in Abak Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping how enterprises operate and how communities experience economic and social change, yet evidence on how small business owners in rural and semi-urban Nigerian local government areas engage with AI remains scarce. This study examined artificial intelligence in business and social development, drawing on business owners in Abak Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model and the Diffusion of Innovation Theory, the study adopted a descriptive survey design. A population of two hundred (200) business owners drawn from five (5) purposively selected business clusters in Abak was used, out of which one hundred and eighty (180) copies of a structured questionnaire were administered and one hundred and seventy (170) were completed, returned and found usable, representing a 94.4 per cent response rate. Data were analysed using mean, standard deviation and chi-square statistics. Findings indicate that the extent of AI adoption among the sampled business owners was moderate, with mobile-based and social-media-embedded AI tools more prevalent than dedicated analytics or automation systems. AI adoption was found to have a significant positive effect on business performance and a significant positive effect on social development in the study area. The study concludes that artificial intelligence, although still at an early diffusion stage among small business owners in Abak, holds considerable promise for enterprise growth and community-level social development where awareness, infrastructure and skills gaps are addressed. It is recommended that government agencies, financial institutions and polytechnic-based entrepreneurship centres intensify digital and AI-literacy interventions targeted at small business owners in semi-urban within the local government areas.

title: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Reasoning Engine for Early Detection of Pediatric Growth Disorders
abstract: Routine childhood growth surveillance is a cornerstone of pediatric care. Growth pattern abnormalities are often early manifestations of chronic disease. Yet subtle abnormalities are frequently underrecognized, leading to diagnostic delays and avoidable morbidity. We introduce SPROUT (System for Pediatric Recognition Of Undiagnosed Trajectories), a generalized, multi-agent large language model (LLM) reasoning system designed to identify a broad spectrum of pediatric growth-related conditions from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) earlier than standard clinical practice. Using a large pediatric primary care EHR dataset, we developed and validated SPROUT as a two-stage system. First, a highly specific LLM screener flags concerning longitudinal growth patterns. Second, an Orchestrator module coordinates a multidisciplinary panel of LLM agents to generate a ranked differential diagnosis. To correct systemic reasoning errors, a Trainer module injects meta-knowledge into the panel via a dedicated "Learner" agent. Diagnostic capability was evaluated using a walk-forward, visit-by-visit simulation leading up to the diagnosis date. The SPROUT screener model achieved 98% (83/85) specificity and 28% (9/32) sensitivity on a gold-standard dataset of pediatric primary care patients when evaluated one year before the index date, and 100% specificity and 47% sensitivity when evaluated using longitudinal data up to the day of diagnosis. When applied to 300 control patients (i.e., healthy or undiagnosed), the screener flagged 15. Subsequent expert panel review confirmed high suspicion for undiagnosed pathology in 33% (5/15) of these cases. In chronological walk-forward validation on disease cases, the diagnostic engine identified conditions well before standard-of-care documentation. One year prior to clinical diagnosis, the system achieved sensitivities of 81% for type 1 diabetes mellitus, 56% for pituitary disorders, and 44% for celiac disease. The SPROUT multi-agent system demonstrates the ability to detect a significant portion of latent growth-related pediatric conditions months to years before current clinical standards while minimizing false positives. These results support its potential as a decision support tool for reducing diagnostic delays in pediatric care.

title: Effect of AI Voice Assistants’ Pause Duration on Recommendation Acceptance : Mediation of Perceived AI Deliberation and Moderation of Recommendation Type
abstract: 이 연구는 AI 음성 어시스턴트의 추천 발화 전 휴지(pause)가 사용자의 추천 수용에 미치는 영향을 검증했다. 60명을 대상으로 3(휴지: 0.2초/1.0초/3.0초)×2(추천 유형: 영화/보험) 혼합 설계 실험과 사후 인터뷰를 수행했다. 휴지 시간과 추천 수용 간의 비선형(U자형) 관계는 실용재에서만 유의하고 쾌락재에서는 나타나지 않았다. 실용재에서는 AI 숙고 인식, 즉 사용자의 상황을 헤아려 깊이 생각한 뒤 응답한다는 지각이 핵심 매개기제로 작동하여, 휴지의 영향이 주로 사용자의 심리적 귀인 과정을 거쳐 전달됐다. 이 연구는 발화 내용과 함께 발화 방식 역시 추천 수용에 영향을 미치는 요소임을 확인했고, AI 숙고 인식이라는 새로운 구성개념을 제안했다. 노동 환상 이론과 기대 위반 이론을 AI 음성 맥락으로 확장하였으며, 준언어적 단서의 효과가 추천유형에 따라 달라진다는 점을 밝혔다. 이는 AI 음성 인터페이스 설계에서 추천 유형별 휴지 전략 차별화가 필요함을 보여준다.

title: Bystander-Verifiable Hardware-Attested Recording-State Indicator with Tamper-Evident, Fixed-Interval State Logging
abstract: This is a defensive publication establishing public prior art for a hardware-level architecture that makes a device's visible recording indicator a verifiable, tamper-evident representation of its actual sensor state. A dedicated hardware element monitors sensor activation directly at the electrical level, independent of host system software, and periodically broadcasts cryptographically signed, sequentially numbered state records over an out-of-band channel. This allows a bystander or auditor to independently verify, and retain a dated history of, whether a device's recording indicator has accurately reflected its actual sensor state over time. The author and publisher dedicate this specific invention to the public domain. No patent rights are sought or reserved for the subject matter described.

title: 基于神经网络的非线性几何优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network-based non-linear geometric optimization algorithm. Traditional geometric optimization methods often require extensive manual parameter design, limiting flexibility and potentially producing suboptimal solutions. This work proposes a new approach that leverages neural networks to automatically learn and optimize geometric features, enabling more precise geometric shape design and optimization. We present a framework where a neural network is trained to identify key geometric characteristics within a given set of parameters, and these characteristics are then utilized to guide the optimization process. The algorithm focuses on achieving a better balance between geometric accuracy and computational efficiency. This research represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a robust and automated method for tackling complex geometric optimization problems.

title: Probability-Based Optimization Algorithm for Dynamic Variable Assignment and Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic optimization algorithm designed to enhance machine learning model parameter optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in handling complex data distributions. This algorithm dynamically adjusts parameter values based on probability distributions, mitigating the risk of getting stuck in local optima and promoting better generalization. The core mechanism involves modeling the optimization process as a probabilistic model, evaluating different parameter combinations based on these distributions, and iteratively refining parameters to maximize model performance. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and evaluation through illustrative examples focusing on a specific classification task. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in model accuracy and robustness compared to traditional optimization techniques.

title: Dynamic Modular Self-Organizing Network
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic modular self-organizing network (DMSON) designed to effectively model and control complex systems, particularly within the domains of biological information and complex systems. The DMSON leverages a modular architecture with dynamically adjusted weights and connections between modules, enabling adaptive modeling and control based on input data. A core mechanism centers on the iterative adjustment of these parameters, fostering robust and responsive behavior. This approach offers significant advantages over traditional network models, particularly in situations requiring adaptability and resilience to complex dynamics. The paper details the design, implementation, and evaluation of the DMSON, highlighting its potential applications across diverse fields.

title: Hyperdimensional Computing with Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing hyperdimensional computing by integrating quantum error correction (QEC) codes. Hyperdimensional computing, characterized by its use of high-dimensional vectors (hypervectors) and sparse representations, offers potential advantages in terms of energy efficiency and scalability. However, it is susceptible to noise and errors, limiting its practical applications. This research proposes mapping hypervectors to specific states within a carefully selected QEC code, thereby enabling the detection and correction of these errors. The core claim is that this integration significantly improves the robustness and scalability of hyperdimensional computing. The proposed method leverages the inherent redundancy and error-detecting capabilities of QEC, providing a pathway toward reliable and performant hyperdimensional computation. This paper details the theoretical framework, explores potential QEC code choices, and discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with this combined approach.

title: Title: Modular Quantum Error Correction with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: Quantum information processing, while promising, is inherently susceptible to errors due to the fragile nature of quantum states. Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for achieving reliable quantum computation, but existing protocols often suffer from limitations in their robustness. This paper explores a novel approach to QEC utilizing adaptive thresholding based on observed error patterns, aiming to significantly improve resilience to noise. We propose a dynamic threshold adjustment mechanism that learns a 'noise profile' and adapts the threshold accordingly, providing a more effective and robust solution than traditional fixed thresholds. The core mechanism hinges on a self-learning algorithm that analyzes the quantum state and its evolution to determine the optimal threshold for error detection and correction. This research addresses a fundamental challenge in QEC – the need for adaptive thresholds in the presence of complex noise – and presents a framework for enhancing the overall error correction capabilities of quantum systems. The theoretical underpinnings and implementation details are detailed within the paper.

title: ## Bishop Moss Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bishop Moss Mouse Algorithm (BMMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Bishop moss mice. These remarkable organisms exhibit an efficient and adaptive strategy for locating food sources in complex, spatially-varying environments. BMMA leverages this biological insight to develop a robust optimization technique suitable for tackling challenging problems across various domains. The algorithm incorporates key features of moss mouse foraging, including directional movement, adaptive exploration, and memory-based decision-making. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the position representation, movement strategy, and adaptive parameters. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its effectiveness in converging to optimal or near-optimal solutions for several benchmark problems. The algorithm's design prioritizes efficiency and adaptability, offering a promising alternative to existing metaheuristic methods. Specifically, we explore the algorithm's convergence properties and its ability to handle multimodal landscapes, demonstrating its potential for solving complex optimization tasks where traditional methods may struggle. The overall aim of this work is to introduce a biologically-inspired approach to metaheuristic optimization with demonstrable performance.

title: SESTINA v1.0: Exact Inference, Robust Evaluation, and Adversarial Testing in Six-Player Canadian Fish
abstract: Six-player Canadian Fish is a decentralised imperfect-information team game in which every action is public, so the hidden state reduces to the initial deal and the posterior over that deal can be computed exactly. We develop and evaluate SESTINA v1.0, the strongest configuration produced in this project’s FishBot lineage. It combines an approximate Sinkhorn fit to that posterior, started from a fitted policy prior, with a linear ask and declaration policy, a public-history tie-breaking rule that preserves common knowledge among teammates, a half-suit contestation weighting, a deduction-state stall detector in place of an event-count termination rule, and a guarded determinized test-time search. Evaluation follows a protocol registered in advance and run on sealed holdout material, using duplicate deal blocks, deal-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, replication across two disjoint deal banks as an advance-specified criterion, calibrated detection floors, and mechanical side-channel controls. Against F-cheap, the cheapest configuration genuinely on the v0.6 frontier and the registered comparison target, SESTINA v1.0 achieves a +3.33 percentage-point win-rate edge (95% CI [+2.88, +3.78]) over 48,000 sealed games, with the sign replicating on both banks. The advantage persists under cross-play between independently trained runs and eight rule dialects. Under partner substitution against a v0.5 opponent 6 of 7 changed-partner rows stay positive, but the worst is −0.19 [−1.04, +0.67], which that battery does not resolve against the registered −1.00 collapse threshold. Separately, none of eight independently constructed adversarial searches found a positive edge at the tested budgets. SESTINA v1.0 does not, however, measurably outperform a composite configuration assembled earlier in the same programme (+0.15 pp, 95% CI [−0.29, +0.59]), indicating that the architecture work which followed added no measurable strength. Over a shared 31-member opponent panel SESTINA v1.0’s worst cell is −0.04 pp [−1.41, +1.33], which does not replicate in sign, and it is 3rd of four on minimax regret. Four candidate mechanisms failed to produce measurable improvement at this resolution. At the calibrated resolution of this evaluation the tested policy class appears locally flat, and we state what evidence a near-optimality claim would require.

title: Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Algorithm (APAA) designed to automatically optimize model parameters for improved performance and adaptability to new data. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex environments and rapidly evolving datasets. The APAA leverages an adaptive learning approach, allowing the model to dynamically adjust its parameters based on observed data, resulting in enhanced predictive accuracy and robustness. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a self-learning strategy that iteratively refines parameter values to achieve optimal model behavior. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and empirical evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of machine learning tasks.

title: ## Berthe's Mouse Lemur: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Mouse Lemur Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Berthe's Mouse Lemur, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Berthe, a well-studied mouse lemur species. Mouse lemurs exhibit remarkable adaptive strategies for finding food in complex and uncertain environments. This paper leverages these strategies – specifically, their opportunistic exploration, risk-averse decision-making, and efficient path planning – to develop a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm. Berthe's Mouse Lemur employs a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of adaptive exploration, a stochastic risk assessment mechanism, and a path-based movement strategy. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with relatively low computational cost. We propose a novel exploration strategy based on the concept of "opportunistic foraging," where particles dynamically adjust their search radius based on the perceived density of promising regions. Furthermore, we introduce a risk-averse component that penalizes particles for moving towards areas with high uncertainty, promoting a more stable and reliable search. Finally, the path-based movement strategy simulates the mouse lemur's efficient route planning, optimizing the movement of particles towards the global optimum.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Causal Inference
abstract: Causal inference is a fundamental problem in artificial intelligence, requiring the ability to understand and reason about cause-and-effect relationships. Traditional approaches, relying solely on deep learning or symbolic methods, often face significant challenges. Deep learning models can struggle to generalize causal relationships from observed data, while symbolic systems require extensive hand-crafted knowledge and are often brittle when confronted with noisy or incomplete data. This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic approach to causal inference that combines the strengths of both paradigms. We introduce a hybrid system where a deep neural network learns statistical correlations from data, and a symbolic reasoning engine, specifically a causal Bayesian network, utilizes these correlations alongside domain knowledge to infer causal relationships. The core of our system lies in the integration of these two components, enabling a more robust, interpretable, and adaptable solution for causal reasoning. The system is designed to overcome the limitations of purely data-driven or purely symbolic approaches, ultimately leading to improved performance in complex causal scenarios. We explore the architecture and key components of this system, laying the groundwork for future research and development in this critical area.

title: Quantum-Inspired Kernel Learning for Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to feature extraction utilizing quantum-inspired kernel learning. Traditional kernel methods suffer from significant computational burdens and the need for meticulous kernel parameter tuning. We propose a technique that leverages concepts from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference, to generate kernels capable of efficiently capturing intricate feature relationships within data. Our method dynamically adapts kernel parameters based on data characteristics, offering a more robust and computationally efficient alternative. The core idea is to mimic the probabilistic nature of quantum states to create kernels that explore a wider range of possible feature combinations simultaneously. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its key components, highlighting its advantages over conventional kernel learning methods. The primary objective is to reduce the computational complexity associated with kernel learning while maintaining, or even enhancing, the accuracy of feature extraction.

title: ## Banka Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Banka Shrew Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Banka Shrew, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Banka shrew ( *Crocidura bankhursti* ). Banka shrews are known for their unique and efficient foraging strategies, particularly their ability to exploit patchy environments with limited visibility. The algorithm leverages these behavioral characteristics through a novel combination of particle movement strategies, adaptive parameter control, and a dynamic patch exploration mechanism. We detail the algorithm's design, including its core components – the patch concept, movement probabilities, and local search operator. We demonstrate Banka Shrew's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results indicate that Banka Shrew effectively addresses challenges inherent in complex, discontinuous, and multimodal search spaces, demonstrating a robust and adaptable optimization approach. The key formula and notations used within this paper are: `x_i(t)` representing the position of the i-th particle at time t, `v_i(t)` representing the velocity of the i-th particle at time t, `ω_i(t)` representing the weight factor for the i-th particle at time t, `c1` and `c2` representing cognitive and social coefficients, `r1` and `r2` representing random numbers between 0 and 1, `φ_i(t)` representing the influence of the cognitive component, and `φ_so(t)` representing the influence of the social component.

title: Symbolic Regression with Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to mathematical discovery by integrating symbolic regression with automated theorem proving. The core idea is to leverage the ability of symbolic regression to efficiently explore the space of potential mathematical equations and then utilize the rigorous verification capabilities of automated theorem provers to ensure the accuracy and consistency of the discovered equations. We present a framework where a symbolic regression engine generates candidate equations, and these candidates are subsequently subjected to verification by an automated theorem prover. This synergistic combination allows for the identification of equations that not only fit the data but also adhere to mathematical constraints, leading to more reliable and robust mathematical models. The framework is designed to address limitations of traditional symbolic regression, which often struggles with the verification of generated equations, and the limitations of automated theorem proving, which frequently require manual input of initial hypotheses. We outline the architecture of this system, discuss the integration strategies, and highlight the potential benefits of this combined approach for various applications, including scientific discovery, engineering design, and data analysis.

title: 基于多尺度信息理论的算法复杂度分析
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm complexity analysis leveraging the principles of multi-scale information theory. Traditional algorithm analysis often focuses predominantly on time complexity, neglecting crucial aspects such as space complexity and communication complexity. This research introduces a framework that decomposes algorithms into multiple scales, quantifying the information content associated with each scale. This holistic approach provides a more nuanced and accurate assessment of algorithmic complexity, offering insights beyond the limitations of single-dimensional analysis. The core of this method lies in applying information-theoretic concepts – entropy, mutual information, and related measures – to each scale to determine the associated complexity. This allows for a more complete understanding of the computational resources required by an algorithm. We demonstrate the application of this framework through theoretical examples, illustrating its ability to capture complexities that are often overlooked in conventional methods. The results highlight the potential for improved algorithm design and optimization based on a multi-faceted complexity perspective.

This work proposes a novel paradigm utilizing superposition, allowing a quantum system to represent and manipulate multiple states simultaneously. abstract: This paper introduces Argentine Serotine, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Argentine Serotine (*Euthanopepla australis*). The algorithm mimics this behavior through a combination of local search, population-based exploration, and adaptive parameter control. Specifically, Argentine Serotine employs a novel "memory-guided exploration" mechanism, where previously successful search regions are given preferential treatment during the exploration phase. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The design principles and mathematical framework of Argentine Serotine are thoroughly described, highlighting its key features and potential applications in diverse optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm relies on maintaining a "memory" of promising solution regions, dynamically adjusting exploration and exploitation rates based on the observed success rates of these regions. The algorithm's objective is to minimize the cost function, denoted as *C(x)*, where *x* represents the decision variables. The performance is assessed using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

title: Ant-Inspired Adaptive Search (AIAS): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Ant Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Ant-Inspired Adaptive Search (AIAS), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of ants. AIAS mimics the efficient trail-laying and adaptive decision-making processes of ants to navigate complex search spaces and find optimal solutions. The algorithm incorporates adaptive pheromone update rules, a novel position update mechanism based on ant step size variation, and a local search strategy to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. Unlike traditional ant colony optimization algorithms, AIAS dynamically adjusts parameters based on the swarm's performance, leading to improved convergence rates and robustness. The core innovation lies in the adaptive pheromone mechanism which responds to both solution quality and the diversity of the search space. This paper presents the algorithm's theoretical foundation, design principles, and a detailed explanation of its components.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory Access
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed memory access leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. The core concept is to construct a distributed network of quantum processors interconnected via entangled states. This architecture aims to circumvent the limitations of conventional data transfer methodologies in traditional computer architectures, specifically addressing the bottleneck inherent in distance-based data transmission. The proposed system offers the theoretical possibility of superluminal data access – accessing data stored on any processor within the network instantaneously through entanglement correlation, without requiring physical data transfer. We detail the theoretical framework, outlining the key components and operational principles of such a system. The focus is on the architectural design and the mathematical formulation of the entanglement-based memory access protocol, highlighting the potential for fundamentally transforming data processing paradigms. This work presents a foundational exploration of this concept, paving the way for future research into realizing entanglement-driven distributed memory. ---

title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Regularization
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian geometric chaos theory to construct a dynamic regularization framework. Geometric chaos, characterized by unpredictable fluctuations in a system's behavior, presents a significant challenge for traditional statistical modeling. We propose a Bayesian approach that automatically adjusts regularization parameters based on observed curvature, thereby promoting a more stable and robust predictive model. The core mechanism involves extending Bayesian inference to a geometric chaos context, enabling the system to adapt to inherent instability and enhance predictive accuracy. This research addresses limitations of existing techniques by incorporating a dynamic regularization strategy, offering a novel pathway for modeling complex, unpredictable systems.

title: Topology-Based Cryptography with Adaptive Key Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptographic system leveraging topology to generate keys dynamically, adapting to user behavior. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on static keys, which are vulnerable to attack if the key is compromised. This work proposes a system that constructs a topological graph representing the key and data, allowing the graph to evolve based on user interactions, thereby enhancing security and resilience. We detail the design of the system, focusing on the mathematical foundations and implementation considerations. The core claim is that this system provides a more robust cryptographic solution than existing approaches by incorporating dynamic graph modifications. This research explores the potential of topology for key management and demonstrates a framework for adaptive key generation using a graph-based approach. The system's effectiveness will be evaluated through simulations and potential testing of cryptographic strength.

title: Abo Butterfly Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Abo Butterfly Bat
abstract: This paper presents Abo Butterfly Bat (ABB), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Abo butterfly bat. ABB combines elements from the butterfly bat algorithm (BBA) with a modified exploration-exploitation strategy and a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism. The core of ABB lies in its dynamic adjustment of the 'flight speed' and 'wing beat frequency' parameters, mimicking the bat's ability to adapt its flight based on environmental conditions and food availability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABB through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and Brent's test function. The results indicate that ABB consistently outperforms or achieves comparable performance to existing metaheuristic algorithms such as the BBA and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. This research contributes a new algorithmic approach to the field of metaheuristic optimization, offering a potentially valuable tool for tackling complex optimization challenges.

abstract: Neural networks are increasingly deployed in diverse applications, demanding optimized performance across a broad range of tasks. title: Allen's Yellow Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Echolocation
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Allen's Yellow Bat" (AYB), inspired by the echolocation behavior of Allen's yellow bats. The algorithm leverages the bat's efficient search strategy for insect detection in complex environments. AYB utilizes a modified version of the bat algorithm, incorporating a dynamic parameter adjustment scheme based on the bat's pulse rate and frequency modulation, mimicking the bat's adaptive response to varying environmental conditions. The core of the algorithm revolves around a fitness evaluation function that simulates the bat's ability to detect prey by emitting pulses and analyzing the reflected echoes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AYB through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and Sphere function. The results indicate that AYB outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution accuracy. Further, we analyze the algorithm's adaptability and robustness across different problem landscapes. The algorithm's adaptability is evaluated through varying parameter settings and problem complexities. Finally, we discuss potential extensions and future research directions for AYB and related bio-inspired optimization techniques.

title: Algorithmic Authorship, Data Sovereignty, And Intellectual Property Rights: Navigating the Intersection of Law, Science, And Society in the
abstract: Abstract The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), data science, and legal frameworks has created a profound crisis within global and domestic Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) regimes. Traditionally, copyright and patent laws were constructed around the central premise of human agency, recognizing intellectual labor as an extension of human dignity and personality. This paper examines the multidisciplinary intersection of law, computer science, and social sciences regarding IPR. It deconstructs three critical dilemmas: (1) the legal status of AI-generated works and the "human author" requirement under copyright law; (2) the patentability of AI-invented subject matter and the doctrine of the "Person Having Ordinary Skill in the Art" (PHOSITA); and (3) the socio-economic implications of training data scraping, digital commons, and data sovereignty. By analyzing statutory provisions, recent judicial precedents across jurisdictions, and socio-legal frameworks, this study highlights the inadequacy of existing legal doctrines to address non-human innovation. The paper proposes a balanced normative framework incorporating a sui generis legal model for AI outputs, compulsory licensing for dataset training, and transparent algorithmic disclosure to foster technological innovation while protecting human creators and public domain integrity.

title: A Large Language Model-based Self-analysis Support Dialogue System for Job-hunting Students
abstract: To prevent mismatches in job hunting, self-analysis is widely encouraged. However, conventional methodssuch as worksheets require high metacognitive ability and tend to focus on the“ present self ”, making it difficult forstudents to examine their decisions in relation to future goals and life design. This study introduces a time perspectivein which students reflect on the present from the standpoint of their future selves, and proposes a dialogue systemthat supports self-analysis by prompting users to notice inconsistencies between their current values and decisionsmade after concretizing a future vision. The system asks job-hunting students to rank evaluation criteria for companyselection as a values list, elicits their future dreams, and then generates staged questions about the consistency betweentheir dreams and current values, as well as the possibility that their values may change after achieving those dreams.It was implemented as a web application with an adaptive probing mechanism based on utterance classification andemotion analysis using voice emotion labels and response intervals. A comparative experiment with 15 engineeringundergraduate job-hunting students showed medium-to-large effect sizes for clarifying work-career and private-lifegoals and for gaining new perspectives, such as work-career goals (Cliff ’s δ = 0.58) and gaining a new perspective(Cliff ’s δ = 0.50). The amount of change in ranked values also tended to increase in the latter half of the dialogue.Given the small sample size, future work should validate the system with a larger, more diverse population and furtherrefine the intervention strategy.

title: Data Preprocessing-based Hybrid LLM-BERT Framework for Automatic TTP Extraction from CTI Documents
abstract: 사이버 위협 인텔리전스(CTI, Cyber Threat Intelligence) 보고서는 비정형 장문 텍스트로 작성되는 경우가 많아, 분석가가 수작업으로 MITRE ATT&CK 기반 TTP(Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures)를 매핑하는 데 상당한 시간과 비용이 소요된다. 문서 단위 다중 라벨 환경에서는 장문 문맥 처리, 희소 라벨 분포, 데이터 노이즈로 자동 추출 성능이 저하된다. 본 연구는 TRAM2와 AnnoCTR 데이터셋에서 URL, IOC 등 노이즈를 체계적으로 제거하고, Kanana-1.5 2.1B와 CySecBERT를 결합한 하이브리드 TTP 추출 프레임워크를 제안한다. LLM으로 텍스트를 입력받아 TTP 후보를 생성하고 BERT로 정밀 검증하는 구조이다. 실험 결과 TRAM2에서는 규칙 기반 노이즈 제거가, AnnoCTR에서는 URL 제거가 최적 성능을 보였다. 하이브리드 구조는 TRAM2, AnnoCTR 모두에서 F1 점수 향상을 보였으며, 특히 Precision 중심의 성능 개선이 두드러졌다.

title: Encoding Compact U(1) Gauge Fields in Bosonic Modes with GKP Stabilization
abstract: Compact lattice gauge theories are formulated in terms of angular variables and integer electric fluxes, while bosonic quantum hardware provides oscillator modes with continuous, unbounded quadratures. We bridge this gap with a one-to-one encoding. After Gauss's law is solved, each remaining gauge degree of freedom is carried by a single oscillator mode, with its interactions built from trigonometric gates, and a Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP)-type stabilizer provides the compactness that the hardware does not. The encoding becomes exact in the limit of infinite squeezing, and at finite squeezing, the leading imperfections act as small, computable shifts of physical observables rather than uncontrolled leakage. We apply the construction to compact QED$_3$ and derive the error budget at finite squeezing, characterizing the leading errors in closed form, and showing that they can be corrected, subtracted, or extrapolated away. We construct syndrome-extraction protocols that detect and remove the displacement component of photon loss, delimit the noise it does not reach, compare two choices of dynamical variables, and collect the scaling of mode count, gate count, and measurement cost. A one-plaquette example reproduces the exact compact-rotor dynamics, and real-time spectroscopy with controlled extrapolations recovers the exponentially small energy splitting between charge sectors, the seed of the monopole physics of the theory, at the percent level against its exact value.

title: Calibrating Small Language Models for Claim Check-Worthiness Detection
abstract: Assessing claim check-worthiness is an essential first step in automated fact-checking pipelines. This work is motivated by a real deployment challenge at an early-stage startup: running large language models (LLMs) over every incoming claim is cost- and latency-prohibitive, yet smaller models sacrifice accuracy. We propose NN-PPI, a pointwise extension of Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI) that calibrates model predictions at inference time as a lightweight post-hoc layer, without re-training the underlying model. NN-PPI achieves weighted F1 gains ranging from 12% to 33.80% depending on the size and performance of the baseline model, bringing SLMs on par with larger LLMs. Beyond few-shot SLMs, NN-PPI further improves a production-deployed fine-tuned model, demonstrating that residual calibration is complementary to supervised fine-tuning. By recovering LLM-level accuracy from models that are an order of magnitude cheaper to serve, it makes accurate check-worthiness detection substantially cheaper to operate at scale. Our code and data can be found at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/arr-claim-worthiness-F237.

title: CM2: Multimodal Cultural Reasoning via an Integrated Multi-Agent Framework
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown remarkable success in STEM domains, where progress is often driven by vertical, step-by-step deduction under relatively stable symbol systems. Their horizontal, interdisciplinary cultural reasoning, however, remains underexplored.We propose CM2, a multi-agent framework grounded in the cognitive pathway of human cultural interpretation. CM2 integrates multimodal perception, retrieval-augmented generation, networked reasoning, gated fusion, and reward-driven feedback.Experiments on CM2D across multiple MLLM backbones show consistent gains over CoT and typical reasoning paradigms; ablations validate each module's contribution, and conflict analyses confirm genuine cross-modal arbitration.

title: Peliteoreettinen Semantiikka Logiikassa
abstract: Tutkielmani käsittelee aihetta Peliteoreettinen semantiika. Määrittelen tämän semantiikan sekä esittelen, kuinka se on ekvivalentti Tarskin totuusmääritelmän kanssa. Peliteoreettinen semantiikka on tapa tulkita kaavojen totuutta peliasetelman avulla, jossa kaksi pelaajaa kilpailevat tiettyjä säännönmukaisuuksia noudattaen, jolloin pelin voittanut pelaaja määrittää kaavan totuusarvon. Tutkielmassa esitellään ensimmäiseksi logiikan syntaksi, ja tämän jälkeen ensimmäisen kertaluvun logiikka. Tämän jälkeen siirrytään tutkimaan peliteoreettista semantiikkaa. Esittelen tämän semantiikan perusidean, siihen liittyviä määritelmiä, tuloksia sekä esimerkkejä. Sitten esitän Tarskin totuusmääritelmän, jotta voisin todistaa päätuloksen: sen, että jokaisen kaavan totuus tietyssä mallissa on sama riippumatta siitä, käytetäänkö peliteoreettista semantiikaa tai Tarskin totuusmääritelmää totuuden määrittämiseen. Seuraavassa kappaleessa esittelen käytännön esimerkkejä, joissa mallinnan tilanteita ensimmäisen kertaluvun logiikalla ja teen väittämiä, joiden totuuksia tutkin peliteoreettisen semantiikan menetelmillä. Lisäksi määrittelen joillekin peleille voittostrategioita, jotka ovat seurauksia totuuden tutkimisesta. Viimeisessä kappaleessa pohdin sitä, miten ensimmäisen kertaluvun logiikkaa voisi opettaa lukiolaisille, sekä arvioin näyttämieni esimerkkien mielekkyyttä pedagogisessa mielessä.
