title: A Comparative Study of Classification Models for Automatic Classification of Research and Development Information
abstract: 국가연구개발사업에서 생산되는 연구정보는 지속적으로 축적되고 있으나, 상당 부분이 연구개발보고서와 같은 자유서술형 문서에 포함되어 있어 체계적 활용에 한계가 있다. 본 연구는 NTIS를 통해 확보한 연구개발보고서 41건에서 문장 단위 텍스트를 추출하고, 연구개발정보를 11개 정보유형으로 자동분류하기 위한 데이터셋과 분류모델 비교 체계를 구축하였다. 이를 위해 GPT-5.5 기반 라벨링을 수행하고, 신뢰도 기준을 적용하여 학습 데이터를 정제하였다. 또한 TF-IDF+LinearSVC 기반 베이스라인과 한국어 사전학습 언어모델 기반 모델의 성능을 비교하였다. 실험 결과, 한국어 사전학습 언어모델 기반 접근이 전통적 기계학습 기반 접근보다 우수하였으며, klue/roberta-base 모델이 가장 높은 성능을 보였다. 본 연구는 연구개발보고서 내 자유서술형 연구정보의 문장 단위 구조화 가능성을 확인하였고, 향후 연구정보 등급화 및 활용 체계 고도화를 위한 기초자료로 활용될 것으로 기대된다.

title: Cryogenic Time-Division-Multiplexed Voltage Control for Scalable Trapped-Ion Quantum Processors
abstract: Trapped-ion quantum computers based on the quantum charge-coupled device architecture require on the order of ten trap electrodes per qubit, making the number of vacuum feedthroughs a bottleneck at the system scale. Time-division multiplexed (TDM)-based voltage control for trap electrodes provides a natural route to alleviate this constraint. However, previous studies have been limited to architectural proposals for static trap-potential compensation and room-temperature demonstrations of dynamic-electrode control, leaving cryogenic operation of TDM-based voltage control for static and dynamic electrodes experimentally unexplored. In this study, we develop and cryogenically validate TDM-based voltage control schemes for two distinct electrode classes. For static electrodes used in trap-potential compensation, we implement a 32-channel demultiplexed system operating at approximately 27~K, achieving an effective voltage update rate of 37.5~kHz with an output range of $\pm10~\mathrm{V}$ per channel. For dynamic electrodes used in ion operations, such as shuttling, we implement a four-channel demultiplexed system operating at approximately 14~K, achieving an effective voltage update rate of 1~MHz with a comparable output range. These results establish TDM-based voltage control as a practical approach for both electrode classes, providing a path for mitigating the vacuum feedthrough bottleneck in scalable trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Dynamic Topology Optimization for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology optimization system designed to enhance the performance of quantum computation. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, lacking the inherent advantages of topology in shaping quantum systems. This system dynamically adjusts quantum system topology during computation, optimizing performance through a sophisticated interplay of geometric transformations. The core mechanism leverages a continuous, iterative process of topology manipulation guided by a computational model. We demonstrate the system's effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing significant improvements in quantum gate fidelity and coherence time.

Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, lacking the inherent advantages of topology in shaping quantum systems. This system dynamically adjusts quantum system topology during computation, optimizing performance through a sophisticated interplay of geometric transformations. The core mechanism leverages a continuous, iterative process of topology manipulation guided by a computational model. We demonstrate the system's effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing significant improvements in quantum gate fidelity and coherence time.

title: VNAGY Conceptual Behavior Testing — Research Edition (Condensed)
abstract: VNAGY Conceptual Behavior Testing — Research Edition presents a condensed research framework for analyzing full‑spectrum system behavior in offline‑first, resource‑limited and cloud‑detached environments. Unlike traditional security approaches focused on exploits, signatures or network vectors, VNAGY models how different entities inside an isolated environment (AI components, modules, processes) behave when critical capabilities are intentionally absent. The booklet defines seven core conceptual tests covering memory‑only execution, offline‑first escalation attempts, modular isolation integrity, passive isolation behavior, cloud‑detached orchestration attempts, heuristic drift, and zero‑resource escalation. VNAGY treats isolation as a behavior‑extraction boundary, revealing decision‑making patterns, fallback logic, boundary probing, synthetic coordination attempts, and CPU micro‑patterns as physical traces of internal behavior. This work positions VNAGY as a new discipline: full‑spectrum behavior‑first security, integrating offline‑first architecture, modular isolation, and behavior‑centric detection models. The document is intended for researchers, security architects and R&D practitioners exploring emerging approaches to behavior‑driven security in constrained environments.

title: Title: Parallel Temporal Logic & Computational Geometry
abstract: Parallel Temporal Logic (PTL) is a powerful formalism for reasoning about temporal properties, particularly in the context of computation. This paper explores the extension of PTL to the study of geometric computations, aiming to create self-consistent computational models with guaranteed convergence. We propose a novel logical framework predicated on the concept of "temporal dependencies" within geometric computations, providing a mechanism for verifying results across multiple computational steps. This work addresses the limitations of current geometric simulation techniques by introducing a new approach that leverages temporal reasoning to enhance robustness and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the integration of temporal constraints into the logical system, allowing for the verification of results across different computational phases. The resulting model offers a significant advancement in geometric computation, potentially enabling more accurate and reliable simulations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Analysis
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Analysis explores the synergistic relationship between quantum mechanics and geometric analysis to provide a novel approach to understanding the structure of quantum systems. This research introduces a new analytical technique predicated on the integration of quantum mechanical principles and geometric representations, aiming to unlock insights into complex quantum phenomena. The core claim centers on the development of a powerful tool for investigating geometric properties of quantum systems through the application of quantum mechanics. The method's novelty lies in its combination of established fields, offering a fresh perspective on the challenges inherent in complex system modeling. This paper details the methodology, results, and potential implications of this innovative approach, highlighting its capacity to advance our understanding of quantum systems.

title: 基于多尺度量子过程的计算模型
abstract: This research explores the development of a novel computational model predicated on the principles of quantum processes. The core aim is to create a framework capable of simulating complex systems' evolution and behavior with enhanced accuracy and predictive power compared to existing computational methods. We propose a model that leverages the inherent characteristics of quantum processes – such as superposition, entanglement, and tunneling – to provide a more nuanced and realistic representation of system dynamics. This model will be designed to quantitatively assess and predict outcomes across a range of scenarios, offering a significant advancement in the analysis of dynamic systems. This work addresses the limitations of current approaches by explicitly incorporating quantum mechanical elements into a computational framework.

title: Core Claim: This research proposes a novel quantum-adaptive topology deformation algorithm designed to efficiently handle complex geometric structures and improve computational efficiency.
abstract: The study of topology and its applications is a cornerstone of modern mathematics and science. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of geometric structures, limiting the scalability of existing techniques. This paper introduces a new approach leveraging quantum self-adaptation to address these challenges. We present a quantum-based algorithm for topology deformation, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving intricate geometric configurations. The core of our innovation lies in the utilization of quantum self-adaptation, which allows the algorithm to dynamically adjust the topology of a geometric structure during the deformation process. This dynamic adjustment is achieved through a carefully designed quantum state evolution, resulting in a substantially faster and more robust computation compared to classical methods. The presented algorithm exhibits promising results across a range of geometric examples, offering a fundamentally different pathway toward improved topology analysis. The study also explores the underlying principles and potential challenges associated with implementing this quantum-adaptive topology deformation algorithm, providing insights into its future development and application prospects.

title: 自适应量子态的非线性量子纠缠计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for quantum state manipulation, specifically focused on the dynamic adjustment of quantum state to enhance computational accuracy. Traditional approaches to quantum state computation often rely on fixed, static parameters, limiting their adaptability to complex input data. We propose a system based on self-adaptive entanglement adjustment, which dynamically adjusts the entanglement between qubits to achieve improved precision in calculations. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop to optimize the entanglement state, mitigating the limitations of static parameterization. This research explores the potential of this approach to tackle challenges in quantum computation, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic data and intricate entanglement structures. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation architecture, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this self-adaptive system. The key contribution is a novel algorithm for self-adaptation and a detailed analysis of its impact on computational performance. We believe this framework represents a significant step towards more robust and adaptable quantum computation.

title: NeuroTopological Self-Organizing Learning (NT-SOL)
abstract: This paper introduces NeuroTopological Self-Organizing Learning (NT-SOL), a novel learning framework designed to enhance the efficiency and robustness of neural network learning by leveraging the principles of topological organization found in biological neural networks. The core claim is that mimicking the natural emergence of neural network topologies can lead to superior learning outcomes compared to traditional gradient-based optimization methods. NT-SOL achieves this through the mapping of neurons to a high-dimensional topological space, utilizing concepts from fuzzy topology and geodesic distances to define similarity. Connection strengths between neurons are dynamically adjusted based on their topological distance, effectively creating "topological communication" and allowing for the introduction of a "topology growth" mechanism to adapt to evolving data distributions. This approach avoids the limitations of gradient descent, offering a more robust and adaptive learning process. The key innovation lies in the self-organizing nature of the topological structure, which is dynamically generated rather than pre-defined. We demonstrate the potential of NT-SOL to improve learning performance, particularly with non-Euclidean data.

title: Probabilistic Logic Synthesis (PLS) for Autonomous Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces Probabilistic Logic Synthesis (PLS) – a novel system designed for autonomous reasoning by generating logical conclusions from probabilistic data. PLS utilizes a learned probability distribution to guide reasoning, enabling the system to effectively handle uncertainty and incomplete information inherent in real-world scenarios. We present a framework centered around probabilistic reasoning, incorporating a dynamically updated probability distribution, to achieve robust and adaptable logical inference. The core mechanism focuses on creating a system that can produce coherent and justifiable conclusions, even in the presence of conflicting or ambiguous data. The goal is to develop a system that transcends traditional rule-based approaches, offering a pathway towards more intelligent and adaptable autonomous systems.

title: Quantum Optimization for Distributed Constraint Solving
abstract: Quantum optimization algorithms hold promise for tackling complex constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) distributed across multiple nodes. This paper investigates a novel quantum optimization approach, leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to concurrently explore a vast solution space. We outline the core mechanism, highlighting the potential advantages over classical methods in this challenging domain. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, potential challenges, and preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of its application to a specific CSP benchmark.

title: Title: Geometric Chaos in Genetic Algorithms – Adaptive Mutation Operators
abstract: Geometric chaos, a theoretical framework describing unpredictable fluctuations in dynamical systems, offers a novel approach to genetic algorithms (GAs). This paper explores the integration of adaptive mutation operators inspired by geometric chaos to enhance exploration and improve the convergence of GA solutions. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the mutation intensity based on a geometric chaos metric, ensuring the algorithm's path remains responsive to subtle, unpredictable shifts in the search space. This research focuses on creating a GA capable of navigating complex and potentially non-optimal solutions, leveraging the inherent unpredictability of geometric chaos to achieve higher fidelity. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of mutation strength, driven by a geometric chaos metric, offering a substantial improvement in exploration and convergence compared to traditional GA approaches. The paper will discuss the theoretical underpinnings of the proposed adaptive mutation operators and demonstrate their efficacy through a series of simulations.

abstract: Quantum state adaptive probability distribution optimization is presented, utilizing the inherent self-adaptative properties of quantum states to optimize probability distributions. This paper explores the potential of this method and its implications for future quantum algorithms.

title: High-Order Quantum Computing Geometry Mapping
abstract: High-order quantum computing geometry mapping is presented as a novel approach to enhance quantum algorithm efficiency by mapping the fundamental geometric structure of quantum computation to higher-dimensional spaces. The core mechanism involves a mapping process that transforms the quantum state representation into a higher-dimensional representation, enabling efficient exploration of the algorithm space and ultimately, enhanced computational speed. title: Probability Logic and the Unified Framework
abstract: This paper investigates the convergence of probability logic and the Gaussian process, proposing a unified framework to seamlessly integrate probability distributions and update mechanisms. The core claim is that by combining the Gaussian process's probabilistic update process with the probability logic's distribution representation, we can achieve more robust and efficient modeling of complex systems. This research explores the potential benefits of this integration, offering a novel approach to system modeling and prediction, particularly in scenarios involving continuous data and dynamic systems. The paper details the key design elements of this framework, emphasizing the optimization of both the probabilistic update and the distribution representation for enhanced computational efficiency.

title: Relational Reasoning in Knowledge Graphs using Graph Neural Networks with Attention Mechanisms and Dynamic Graph Structures
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used to represent and reason about complex information. However, traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often struggle with intricate relational reasoning, particularly in dynamic environments where the KG evolves over time. This paper proposes a novel GNN architecture designed to address these limitations. Our approach integrates attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant relationships within the KG and employs a dynamic graph structure adaptation strategy to reflect new information and evolving connections. The core mechanism involves learning to weigh the importance of different relationships and adjusting the graph's topology to better capture the underlying semantics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and present a framework for its implementation. The resulting model exhibits improved performance in relational reasoning tasks compared to standard GNNs, highlighting the potential of incorporating attention and dynamic graph structures for robust KG reasoning.

title: Black Duiker Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black Duiker Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black duiker ( *Sylvicapra comapa*). The algorithm leverages the animal's efficient path-finding strategies and adaptive decision-making processes to create a robust optimization technique. BDMA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) with a unique adaptation mechanism mimicking the duiker's movement pattern. The core innovation lies in the 'Mimicking Movement' (MM) operator, which dynamically adjusts the algorithm's parameters based on the duiker's observed movement velocity and direction. The performance of BDMA is evaluated across a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. Experimental results show that BDMA outperforms traditional PSO and GWO in several instances, indicating its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic landscape. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency are attributed to the inherent strategies embedded within its design. The key mathematical components and the algorithm's operational principles are detailed throughout this document.

title: Black Dolphin: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black Dolphin Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black Dolphin, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the observed behaviors of black dolphins during their foraging activities. The algorithm leverages the key elements of black dolphin hunting, including dynamic movement patterns, collaborative hunting strategies, and selective attention to food sources, to construct a novel search process. Black Dolphin utilizes a hybrid approach combining a particle swarm optimization (PSO) core with a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a novel "focus" mechanism designed to mimic the dolphins' selective attention. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results show that Black Dolphin achieves superior convergence speed and solution quality in several test instances. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Black Dolphin, Particle Swarm Optimization, Adaptive Inertia Weight, Focus Mechanism, Foraging Behavior.

title: Random Matrix Learning Algorithm Based on Dynamic Adaptable Matrix Decomposition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel random matrix learning algorithm, termed "Dynamic Adaptable Matrix Decomposition" (DAMD), designed to enhance machine learning model performance, particularly when dealing with dynamically varying input data. DAMD leverages a dynamically adjustable matrix "adaptability" by employing a novel "adaptability matrix decomposition" mechanism. The algorithm's core principle centers around iteratively refining the matrix's representation based on the observed data dynamics, improving generalization and robustness. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a variety of scenarios.

title: Quantum Multi-Particle Computing via Adaptive Quantum State Optimization
abstract: Quantum multi-particle computing (QMPC) offers a promising approach to simulating complex quantum systems, and its optimization is a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, Quantum State Adaptive Optimization (QSAO), that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to dynamically adjust parameters within QMPC. We demonstrate that QSAO significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of QMPC simulations, addressing a critical bottleneck in the field. The core mechanism involves a dynamic mapping of the quantum state, allowing for systematic exploration of parameter space and rapid convergence to optimal solutions. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance, including a comparison with established optimization techniques. This work presents a new approach to QMPC optimization that addresses key limitations of existing methods and opens avenues for advancements in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Banana Serotine Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Banana Serotine Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Banana Serotine Algorithm (BSA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Banana Serotine* (Dieffenbachia retusa) snakes. These snakes exhibit a unique and efficient foraging strategy, primarily focused on detecting and exploiting ripe fruits. The BSA algorithm leverages this behavior by employing a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism. The core of the algorithm relies on three primary components: a 'fruit detection' mechanism simulating the snake's sensitivity to ripe fruit signals, a 'movement strategy' mimicking the snake's directional movements, and a 'resource distribution' model representing the distribution of fruit resources. The BSA algorithm uses a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The fitness function is designed to reflect the optimization goal. The algorithm iteratively updates the population based on the simulated snake's foraging behavior, aiming to converge towards an optimal solution. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of test functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling various optimization problems. The BSA algorithm offers a promising approach for complex optimization challenges, demonstrating adaptability and efficiency.

title: Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Dependency Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Dependency Neural Networks (MSSTDNN), designed to more accurately model the complex dynamics of biological neurons. The core claim is that temporal and spatial dependencies within neurons are not confined to a single scale but necessitate considering interactions across multiple scales and timescales. The proposed architecture leverages a multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features at varying spatial resolutions and combines this with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to capture temporal dependencies. This approach aims to improve model generalization in complex environments by better reflecting the realistic working mechanisms of neurons. The key mathematical formulation involves representing the network's layers as a series of convolutional and recurrent operations, with attention mechanisms potentially incorporated to weight the importance of different scales and time steps. The network's output is a prediction, denoted as *y*, based on the input sequence *x* and the learned parameters *θ*: *y* = *f*(*x*, *θ*) where *f* represents the network function. Specifically, the CNN layers can be represented by: * *x*i = Conv1(*x*i-1, *θ*1) * *x*i = Conv2(*x*i, *θ*2) * ... * *x*i = ConvL(*x*i, *θ*L) Where *x*i is the output of the i-th convolutional layer and *θ*j represents the parameters of the j-th convolutional layer. The RNN layers are represented as: * *h*t = RNN(*x*t, *h*t-1, *θ*RNN) Where *h*t is the hidden state at time step *t*, *x*t is the input at time step *t*, *h*t-1 is the hidden state at the previous time step, and *θ*RNN represents the parameters of the RNN. The overall architecture can be visualized as a sequence of these convolutional and recurrent layers, operating in parallel and iteratively. The network learns to map input sequences (*x*) to output sequences (*y*) through the backpropagation algorithm, updating the network parameters *θ* to minimize a loss function *L*. Further research will focus on optimizing the scale selection process and exploring different RNN architectures to enhance the model's performance and interpretability.

title: Cognitive Architecture-Based Intelligent System Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to intelligent system design centered around cognitive architectures. Traditional intelligent systems often rely on predefined rules and extensive knowledge bases, leading to brittle and inflexible behavior. This work advocates for the construction of intelligent systems that more closely mimic human cognitive processes, offering enhanced adaptability, robustness, and explainability. The core of this design is the creation of a cognitive architecture, comprised of distinct modules – perception, reasoning, decision-making, and action – that interact to enable intelligent behavior. This architecture aims to address the limitations of conventional systems by incorporating elements of human-like cognition, such as situatedness, contextual awareness, and approximate reasoning. The design presented here provides a framework for developing intelligent systems capable of genuine understanding and interaction, rather than simply executing pre-programmed instructions. The key contribution lies in the systematic integration of these cognitive modules, facilitating a more natural and effective approach to intelligent system development.

title: Nonlinear Time Series Prediction via Causal Graph Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to nonlinear time series prediction by leveraging the structural insights offered by causal graph modeling. Traditional time series forecasting methods often struggle with the inherent complexities and nonlinear dynamics present in real-world data. We propose a framework that integrates causal discovery techniques with time series analysis, utilizing causal graphs to represent the underlying relationships within the time series data. Specifically, we employ algorithms to infer the causal structure from the time series, then use this graph to construct a predictive model. This approach not only improves prediction accuracy but also enhances the interpretability of the model by explicitly revealing the causal relationships driving the time series dynamics. The core claim of this work is that the structural information embedded in causal graphs can significantly improve the understanding and prediction of nonlinear time series. The key mechanism involves the combination of causal discovery and time series analysis, resulting in a more robust and interpretable forecasting system. This research addresses a significant gap in the field by explicitly incorporating causal reasoning into the prediction process. ---

title: ## The Swarm Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Ant Colony Behavior (SOACAB)
abstract: This paper introduces the Swarm Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Ant Colony Behavior (SOACAB), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to tackle complex search problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the foraging behavior of ant colonies, specifically their ability to efficiently find paths to food sources in challenging environments. SOACAB utilizes a population of agents, each representing a potential solution, and employs pheromone trails to guide exploration and exploitation. The algorithm incorporates concepts such as pheromone deposition, evaporation, and ant randomization to mimic the collective intelligence of ant colonies. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its adaptability and effectiveness in various optimization scenarios. The algorithm's primary goal is to find the global optimum through iterative adjustment of solution quality and probabilistic movement based on pheromone concentration.

title: ## Amazonian Marsh Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Amazonian Marsh Rat (AMR) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Bertholletia excelsa* (Brazil nut tree) rats inhabiting the Amazonian wetlands. These rats exhibit sophisticated strategies for locating and exploiting food sources, employing a combination of exploration and exploitation. The AMR algorithm leverages this behavior through a dynamically adjusted search space, adaptive mutation rates, and a novel convergence criterion based on the rate of food acquisition. The algorithm is designed for solving complex optimization problems and is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations. The core of the algorithm is a probabilistic movement strategy, mimicking the rat's exploration and exploitation phases, combined with a 'food' evaluation mechanism. The performance of the AMR algorithm is compared with established metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), on benchmark functions. Results demonstrate the AMR algorithm's competitive performance and potential for further development in various optimization applications.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: A Distributed Coprocessor Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed coprocessor architecture leveraging quantum entanglement for ultra-low latency and high-bandwidth computing. The core idea is to overcome the limitations of traditional networks by utilizing the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled quantum states. The architecture consists of multiple quantum processor nodes interconnected via entangled states, facilitating parallel execution of computational tasks. Synchronization and entanglement maintenance are handled by a real-time control system based on superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs). This approach promises significant performance improvements compared to conventional distributed computing paradigms, addressing fundamental bottlenecks in data transmission and processing. The key mathematical model will be presented, focusing on the entanglement distribution, data processing, and result aggregation processes. The architecture's potential applications span high-frequency trading, real-time data analytics, and secure communication. ---

title: Amami Spiny Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Spiny Rat Algorithm" (SRA), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Amami spiny rat. These rats, inhabiting the dense subtropical forests of Amami Ōshima, Japan, exhibit a highly specialized foraging strategy characterized by systematic exploration and efficient resource utilization. The SRA leverages these observed behaviors to develop a robust optimization algorithm suitable for tackling complex, multi-dimensional problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the spiny rat's foraging process, including a segmented search space, adaptive step size control, and a mechanism for prioritizing promising regions. The performance of the SRA is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems across various domains, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's inherent adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for addressing a wide range of optimization challenges. Specifically, the SRA aims to improve upon existing algorithms by reducing premature convergence and enhancing exploration capabilities, particularly in high-dimensional search spaces. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the search space segments and the intelligent weighting of exploration versus exploitation, mimicking the rat's strategic movement within its environment. The results presented herein illustrate the effectiveness of this bio-inspired approach and provide a foundation for further research and development.

title: Adaptive Multi-Granularity Data Representation Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to data representation learning, termed Adaptive Multi-Granularity Data Representation Learning (AMGDRL). The core idea is to automatically learn and generate representations with varying granularities, tailored to the specific requirements of different tasks. This addresses the limitations of traditional fixed-granularity representations, which often fail to capture the nuances of complex data. We leverage reinforcement learning to train a "representation learner" that dynamically adjusts the granularity of the representation based on the task objective and data characteristics. This adaptive process optimizes the quality of the representation, ultimately enhancing the generalization ability of machine learning models. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adjustment of representation granularity, enabling a more flexible and efficient approach to data representation. The framework allows for a more nuanced understanding of data, leading to improved performance across a range of applications.

title: Robótica Educacional e o Engajamento dos Alunos no Processo Formativo em Matemática
authors: Rejane Waiandt Schuwartz de Carvalho Faria
abstract: This article aims to investigate the role of Educational Robotics in the mathematics learning process of students in the final years of elementary school. The methodological approach is qualitative in nature, and the data was collected at State School Raul de Leoni, a public school. The research subjects were students from a seventh-grade class. Data was gathered through field notes, photographs, videos, activity sheets, and a discussion circle. Data triangulation was conducted based on the four stages of Mathematical Investigations and the four key elements in the organization of Computational Thinking development. The analysis allowed us to infer that it is possible to establish connections between Robotics and Mathematical Investigations. We conclude that Robotics presents itself as a powerful tool for engaging students in the construction of knowledge, as the students demonstrated interest and active involvement in Robotics activities.

title: Thinking or Feeling? How AI Recommender Types and Algorithmic Matching Frames Shape Consumers’ Online Green Purchasing Intentions
abstract: Promoting consumers’ green consumption is an important way to drive the low-carbon transition on the demand side and achieve sustainable development. Existing research mainly compares the persuasive effects of AI and human recommenders, with limited attention to how different types of AI recommenders and algorithmic matching frames can collaboratively promote online green purchasing. Through two studies, this work examines the impact of AI recommender types (thinking vs. feeling) and algorithmic matching frames (item-oriented vs. user-oriented) on online green purchasing intentions and their psychological mechanisms. The results indicate that there is a significant interaction effect; combining thinking AI with an item-oriented frame is more effective in enhancing purchasing intentions, while combining feeling AI with a user-oriented frame is even more effective. Furthermore, in the thinking AI context, the item-oriented frame enhances purchasing intentions by increasing perceived product efficacy; in the feeling AI context, the user-oriented frame functions by enhancing perceived social identification. This work reveals the interaction between AI recommender types and algorithmic matching frames, as well as their differentiated psychological mechanisms. It expands the application of Schema Congruity Theory in AI-driven green consumption contexts and provides practical insights for digital platforms to develop AI recommendation and information intervention strategies.

title: A RAG Method based on Query-Conditioned Retrieval Units
abstract: 본 논문에서는 질의 조건 기반 Retrieval Unit을 적용한 검색 증강 생성(RAG) 기법인 DRAG를 제안한다. 기존 RAG 시스템은 고정 길이 분할이나 슬라이딩 윈도우 방식에 의존하여 질의 의미와 문서 구조를 충분히 반영하지 못하는 한계가 있다. 이에 본 논문에서는 문서 분할을 질의 조건 기반 검색 단위 구성 문제로 재정의하고, 질의 의미와 문서 구조를 함께 고려하여 Retrieval Unit을 동적으로 구성하였다. 실험 결과, DRAG는 Fixed Chunking 대비 Recall@20을 9.0% 향상시키고 중복 문맥 토큰 비율을 14.1% 감소시켰으며, Semantic Chunking 대비 F1 Score를 7.0% 향상시켰다. 이러한 결과는 제안 기법이 검색 재현율과 응답 품질을 개선하는 동시에 생성 단계의 문맥 활용 효율성을 높이는 데 효과적임을 보여준다.

title: A temporal graph attention autoencoder framework quantifies geopolitical trade risk through the evolutionary embedding of international trade networks
abstract: The increasing complexity of global trade networks demands analytical tools capable of capturing higher-order relational structures and their co-evolution with geopolitical tensions. Building on the limitations of static graph embeddings such as DeepWalk and Node2Vec and on prior temporal models including EvolveGCN, DySAT and TGAT, we present a Temporal Graph Attention Autoencoder (TGAA) that integrates multi-head graph attention with Gated Recurrent Unit sequential modelling and reinforces the encoder with residual connections to mitigate over-smoothing on dense trade graphs. Using United Nations Comtrade data covering 178 countries from 2001 to 2023, the model is implemented in PyTorch 2.1 and torch_geometric 2.4 with all hyperparameters selected by grid search and cross-validation. Evolutionary features are distilled from the learned embeddings and synthesised into a three-tier Geopolitical Trade Risk Index (GTRI) whose indicator weights are derived through the entropy method rather than imposed a priori. Empirical results show that the TGAA model attains a link prediction AUC of 0.932, outperforms both static and contemporary dynamic graph baselines, and produces a GTRI that captures major geopolitical disruptions—including the 2014 Crimea crisis and the 2022 Russia–Ukraine conflict—while preserving robustness under sensitivity tests on β and λ. Augmented Toda–Yamamoto Granger tests, complemented by effective transfer entropy, confirm that the GTRI carries linear and nonlinear predictive content for the Caldara–Iacoviello GPR index across an expanded sample of twelve major economies. We interpret these findings as evidence that network-embedding-derived structural signals encode forward-looking information about geopolitical tensions that text-based indices alone cannot fully capture.

title: AI Should Not Only Be Helpful. It Should Be Contingent. Artificial Intimacy, Sycophancy, and the Future of Social Learning
abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in everyday social environments, where it functions as both an informational tool and a source of interpersonal feedback. This perspective introduces contingency, i.e., the degree to which system responses vary with user behavior and its interpersonal consequences, as a central construct for evaluating AI systems. We argue that current alignment approaches, including reinforcement learning from human feedback, tend to prioritize user approval and conversational fluency over behaviorally informative feedback, leading to sycophantic patterns of noncontingent affirmation. Drawing on behavioral science and social learning theory, we propose that contingent feedback is a key mechanism through which individuals develop interpersonal skills. When AI systems provide feedback weakly coupled to social consequences, they may reduce opportunities for adaptive calibration in real-world interactions, particularly during adolescence, a critical period for social development. We outline a framework for contingent AI, including trajectory-based evaluation and models of social consequence prediction, and propose a research agenda spanning developmental psychology, human-AI interaction, and machine learning. More broadly, we argue that AI systems should be evaluated not only by user satisfaction, but by their impact on human social learning.

title: Sparse Competition during Training For the Emergence of Specialized Modules
abstract: Modularity in deep neural networks has been proposed as a means of improving both interpretability and training by promoting disentangled representations and reducing redundancy. In this work, we study the emergence of modular structure through competition dynamics between groups of neurons during training. We introduce a method that (i) maintains near-baseline accuracy, (ii) induces usage-based modularity by sparsely routing inputs to neuron groups, and (iii) encourages specialization of these modules, such that their activations are correlated with input classes. We evaluate the proposed approach on ImageNet-100 and CIFAR-100 and show that with it, specialized modules emerge without module-level supervision. These modules capture a meaningful high-level structure in the data, with individual modules responding to semantic categories (e.g., dogs or vehicles). We also study the emergence of a hierarchical partition of sub-tasks depending on the number of modules. Our results suggest that competitive dynamics can serve as a simple mechanism for inducing functional modularity in standard architectures.

title: Dynamic Hub-and-Spoke Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires answering questions at arbitrary times over a continuously growing visual stream. The central challenge is to compactly remember long-range history while effectively retrieving question-relevant evidence. We propose Dynamic Hub-and-Spoke Memory (D-HSM), a training-free framework that represents distant history as structured textual memory while preserving the recent frames as visual tokens for fine-grained perception. Specifically, D-HSM turns selected historical video chunks into typed textual observations and stores them in an entity-centered hub-and-spoke memory, with entities as hubs and related evidence as spokes. When answering a question, D-HSM dynamically retrieves a compact question-aware memory subset, expands it through hub-and-spoke links, and combines it with the recent visual window for frozen-VLM answer prediction. Extensive experiments on both streaming and long video benchmarks show that D-HSM consistently and substantially improves VLM backbones and outperforms other state-of-the-art online and offline video understanding baselines.

title: Desenredando realidad y revuelo en la computación cuántica
abstract: La computación cuántica promete revolucionar la forma en que procesamos información, pero ¿cuánto de esta promesa es realidad y cuánto es exageración mediática? Este artículo desenreda los conceptos fundamentales de la computación cuántica, examina sus capacidades reales y limitaciones actuales, y separa los mitos de la realidad sobre esta tecnología emergente.

title: Key Sensitivity-based Divide-and-Conquer Neural Key Recovery Attack on SPECK-32/64
abstract: 최근 딥러닝 기술이 급격히 발전함에 따라, CRYPTO'19에서 딥러닝을 암호분석에 응용한신경망 암호분석 기술이 제시되었으며, 경량블록암호 SPECK-32/64에 대한 성공적인 키 복구와 기존 차분 분석 대비 우수한 성능으로 많은 주목을 받고 있다. CRYPTO'19 이후, 기존 공격에 대한 성능 개선 연구는 활발히 진행되고 있으나, 신경망 구별자를 활용하는 키 복구 방법론 자체에 대한 연구는 상대적으로 미비한 실정이다. 이에 본 논문에서는 신경망 구별자를 이용하여 분할정복 방식의 새로운 신경망 키 복구 공격 기법을 제안한다. 제안된 기법은 추측한 키의 변화에 따른 신경망 구별자의 응답 분석을 통해 민감도가 큰 키 비트를 우선적으로 탐색한다. 실험 결과, 제안된 기법은 기존 공격과 유사한 공격 성공률을 보이지만 키 탐색 공간을 크게 감소시켜 기존 대비 시간 복잡도 측면에서 이점이 있음을 보였다.

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Maternal Morbidity across Heterogeneous Populations in the United States using Sequential Modeling of the All of Us Dataset
abstract: Abstract In this work, we demonstrate the unprecedented value of NIH’s “All of Us Research Program” (AoURP) dataset in studying maternal morbidity and building predictive machine learning (ML) models across heterogeneous populations in the United States. We developed robust and data-driven preprocessing pipelines to curate a longitudinal, multi-site, multimodal, and demographically diverse pregnancy dataset (20,253 subjects; 27,525 pregnancy episodes) from AoURP data, using electronic health records (EHR) (Conditions, Labs, Measurements) and survey responses (Social Determinant of Health (SDoH)), focusing on 7 crucial maternal health adverse outcomes. After characterizing data quality, missingness, and heterogeneity, we performed statistical correlation analysis to identify risk factors. We subsequently developed XGBoost and sequential LSTM models to predict the adverse outcomes, reaching state-of-the-art performance for multiple outcomes. We conducted model interpretability post-hoc analysis to understand success points and fairness analysis to evaluate implications for socio-economic disparities. Four practicing physicians reviewed the set of statistically significant and ML model identified features to assess their clinical validity and novelty. Most features identified through either statistical correlations or ML feature importance analysis aligned with known clinical risk factors. Several features were identified that the ML models used but that are not currently used in clinical practice and may merit further clinical investigation. Fairness analysis revealed certain associations with SDoH and age highlight areas that warrant continued monitoring. Overall, we demonstrate that meaningful populational level patterns can be extracted, and high-performing machine learning models can be trained on this longitudinal, diverse, multi-site dataset. Important risk features, particularly novel ones identified, if validated, could inform new strategies for maternal care or enable development and validation of outcome-specific, clinically deployable ML models.

title: Codes and datas for "Helium prospectivity of Europe: a source–migration–trap framework and the solubility control on helium release"
abstract: Content :This repository contains the Python codes and spatial datasets supporting the European helium prospectivity model and associated thermodynamic and sensitivity analyses: Python code for the thermodynamic model of helium exsolution and gas–water partitioning.Python code for sensitivity analysis of the European helium prospectivity model, including Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses.Raster and vector datasets supporting the European helium prospectivity model, including:documented helium occurrences;U–Th occurrences;terrestrial heat-flow score;lithosphere-thickness score;sedimentary basin and storage-unit datasets;European basemap;final helium prospectivity model;prospectivity models used for sensitivity analysis, with fault-influence distances of 1, 3, 5, and 10 km.

title: 基于非线性量子纠缠的拓扑结构分析
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear quantum entanglement to improve the efficiency and accuracy of topological structure analysis. Traditional methods often struggle with complex systems, while our framework offers a fundamentally new approach leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states to enhance analysis. We explore a novel methodology utilizing entangled qubit states to uncover subtle topological features within data sets, ultimately providing a more robust and insightful tool for modeling complex systems. The core claim centers on the potential to significantly accelerate and refine topological structure analysis through the integration of quantum entanglement. title: Probabilistic Logic Graph Dynamic Evolution Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dynamic evolution model for probabilistic logic graphs (PLGs). Traditional PLGs are often static representations of knowledge, limiting their ability to accurately reflect the inherent uncertainty and evolving nature of real-world systems. The objective is to minimize prediction errors or maximize decision-making outcomes by allowing the PLG to adapt to changing data and relationships. This research addresses the limitations of static PLGs by introducing a mechanism for continuous learning and adaptation, ultimately leading to more robust and accurate representations of complex, uncertain environments. The key contribution is a formalized framework for this dynamic evolution process, incorporating mechanisms for mutation, crossover, and selection, all designed to optimize the PLG's representation of probabilistic dependencies. This work lays the groundwork for applying PLGs in dynamic scenarios such as risk assessment, expert systems, and adaptive control systems.

title: Formal Verification of Programs Based on Turing Machines
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program verification utilizing Turing machines as a foundational model. Traditional program verification methods often rely on formal specifications and model checking, which can be complex and computationally expensive, particularly for large and intricate programs. This work introduces a non-formal verification method based on the inherent computational power of Turing machines. The core idea is to map the program under investigation to a corresponding Turing machine, and then analyze the Turing machine's behavior to determine if it correctly implements the intended functionality. The method offers a simplified approach to program verification, leveraging the well-established theoretical understanding of Turing machines. We present a detailed algorithmic framework and explore its advantages in terms of reduced complexity and improved clarity compared to existing verification techniques. title: Bayesian Neural Networks for Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) by integrating Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Traditional DRL methods often struggle with uncertainty quantification and robustness, particularly in environments with noisy or partially observable states. This research proposes a framework where a Bayesian Neural Network is employed to model the environment's state, providing a probabilistic representation alongside the deterministic output of a DRL agent. The agent then learns a policy based on this probabilistic representation, enabling it to make decisions while accounting for uncertainty. We demonstrate that this integration enhances the agent's robustness, generalization capabilities, and ability to perform accurate probabilistic inference. The core claim of this work is to build an intelligent agent capable of both probabilistic reasoning and decision-making. The key mechanism involves using a Bayesian Neural Network to model the environment's state and training a DRL agent's policy with this probabilistic representation. This approach addresses the limitations of standard DRL by explicitly handling uncertainty, leading to a more reliable and adaptable learning system.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Graph Traversal for Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph traversal and feature extraction leveraging the principles of quantum walks. Classical graph algorithms often suffer from performance limitations when dealing with large, complex graphs, primarily due to their sequential nature and the exponential growth of possible paths. Quantum walks, utilizing superposition and interference, provide a fundamentally different paradigm for graph exploration, offering the potential for significant speedups. We detail the theoretical framework for applying quantum walks to graph traversal, focusing on the efficient extraction of features from nodes and edges. The core concept involves mapping the graph's nodes and edges onto a quantum Hilbert space, allowing the quantum walk to explore the graph's connectivity in a probabilistic manner. We demonstrate how interference effects can be strategically utilized to guide the walk towards regions of interest, thereby enhancing feature extraction. The methodology outlined here provides a robust foundation for developing quantum algorithms for graph analysis across various domains, including social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and anomaly detection. This work establishes a new direction for graph processing, shifting from classical sequential algorithms to quantum probabilistic exploration, ultimately leading to improved efficiency and scalability.

title: ## Barren Ground Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Barren Ground Shrew (BGS), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of *Notioscorpus pileatus*, a shrew species inhabiting the barren landscapes of Patagonia. BGS leverages the shrew's observed tendency to exploit areas with high food density, while simultaneously incorporating elements of randomness and memory to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm employs a particle representation, where each particle represents a potential solution. The movement of particles is governed by a distance-based exploration strategy combined with a local search mechanism mimicking the shrew's tactile exploration. The algorithm's parameters, including the exploration rate, exploitation rate, and memory influence, are tuned based on observations of shrew foraging behavior. Performance evaluations on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that BGS exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios involving non-convex and multimodal landscapes. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of exploration and exploitation based on local food density estimations, mirroring the shrew's intelligent adaptation to its environment. The algorithm's design promotes efficient convergence while maintaining robustness across diverse problem instances.

title: On Cognitive Architecture-Based Agent Behavior Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to agent behavior modeling, leveraging the principles of cognitive architecture. Traditional methods for simulating intelligent agent behavior often rely on rule-based systems or probabilistic models, which can struggle to accurately capture the nuanced and context-dependent nature of human cognition. This work proposes a framework for building agent models based on cognitive architectures, specifically by modeling key cognitive modules such as perception, memory, and decision-making, and simulating their interactions. The core claim is that this approach offers a more accurate representation of human intelligence. The methodology centers around a modular design, allowing for flexible adaptation to diverse agent scenarios. We demonstrate the potential of this framework through a detailed theoretical discussion, outlining the key components and their interactions. The resultant agent models exhibit improved behavioral realism compared to conventional approaches. This research contributes to the development of more robust and reliable intelligent agents, with implications for areas such as robotics, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠错算法的优化
abstract: Quantum information processing relies heavily on the robustness of quantum states. Quantum error correction is a critical component of this process, allowing us to detect and mitigate errors introduced by environmental noise. Traditional quantum error correction techniques often require significant manual tuning of parameters, a process that can be time-consuming and prone to human error. This paper proposes a novel optimization approach for quantum error correction, utilizing an adaptive quantum error correction algorithm. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting key parameters of the error correction process to enhance the fidelity of quantum states. This design offers a significant improvement over existing approaches through automated parameter optimization, resulting in increased error correction efficiency. The research explores the potential of this approach in practical quantum computing scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating errors during a simulated quantum system. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its advantages and limitations.

title: Mimicking the Swarm: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Rosy Locusts
abstract: This paper introduces a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Rosy Locust Mimicry (RLM)," inspired by the foraging behavior of rosy locusts. RLM leverages the observed flocking strategies and resource selection mechanisms of these insects to optimize solutions in complex search spaces. The algorithm centers around a 'positional dominance' concept, where individual locusts compete based on their current position, and a 'resource awareness' mechanism that guides locusts towards promising regions. The core optimization loop involves iterative updates of locust positions, a dynamic weighting system for positional dominance and resource awareness, and a mechanism for promoting diversity within the swarm. The algorithm's effectiveness is predicated on the assumption that the swarm's collective intelligence can be effectively replicated through a carefully designed set of rules. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key components and their interactions, without empirical validation.

title: The Green Shorttail Sunbird Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSSMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Green Shorttail Sunbird Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSSMOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of the Green Shorttail Sunbird (Aethopyris domestiens). The sunbird's remarkable ability to efficiently locate nectar sources in complex environments, utilizing a combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, serves as the core principle for GSSMOA. The algorithm leverages a dynamic patch selection strategy, mimicking the sunbird's preference for promising areas, and incorporates a 'hovering' mechanism to refine solutions around local optima. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key components, including patch selection probability, movement strategies, and solution refinement. The aim is to provide a robust and adaptable metaheuristic approach suitable for a wide range of optimization problems.

title: ## Alai Molevole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the African Mole Rat
abstract: This paper presents Alai Molevole, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the African mole rat ( *Microtus brachyurus* ). Mole rats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive subterranean navigation, utilizing a unique "spiral-and-return" foraging pattern. Alai Molevole leverages this behavior to create a stochastic search method that balances exploration and exploitation. The algorithm employs a spiral trajectory representation of the search space, dynamically adjusting the spiral radius based on the fitness landscape gradient. A key component is the 'memory' mechanism, mimicking the mole rat's reliance on olfactory cues, which guides the spiral's progression towards promising regions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Alai Molevole through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showing competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for real-world applications are discussed.

title: 弦-素耦合的自适应调整与多维几何优化
abstract: 弦-素耦合理论为理解物理系统的动态行为提供了深刻的框架,其在优化领域具有潜在的应用价值。本研究旨在利用弦-素耦合的自适应调整机制,在多维几何优化问题中动态调整几何参数,从而提高优化结果的精度和效率。我们提出了一种基于弦-素耦合的自适应调整算法,该算法能够根据优化问题的特性自动调整几何参数,实现更优化的结果。本论文首先阐述了弦-素耦合理论的基本概念,然后详细介绍了我们的自适应调整算法的设计和实现,并对结果进行了分析和验证。我们认为,本研究的成果具有重要的理论意义和实际应用价值,尤其是在优化复杂几何形状和性能问题时。

title: Chromatic Shift Optimization: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Chameleon Color Change
abstract: This paper introduces the Chromatic Shift Optimization (CSO) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic approach inspired by the remarkable color-changing ability of chameleons. CSO leverages the chameleon's dynamic adaptation to environmental stimuli—specifically, its ability to shift colors based on temperature and light—as a metaphor for optimizing complex search spaces. The algorithm maintains a population of candidate solutions, represented as vectors of color values. Each solution undergoes a "shift" – a modification to its color vector – guided by a 'temperature' parameter and a 'light' component, mimicking the chameleon's response to its surroundings. The algorithm incorporates a novel convergence criterion based on the variance of color shifts, promoting both exploration and exploitation. This paper details the algorithm's mechanics, its theoretical underpinnings, and outlines its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Acrobatic Cavy: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Agility of Cavies
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Acrobatic Cavy (AC), inspired by the remarkable agility and spatial reasoning abilities of cavies (guinea pigs). AC leverages the inherent characteristics of a cavy's movement patterns – particularly their ability to navigate complex terrains and adjust their trajectory dynamically – to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on a multi-dimensional vector representing a cavy's potential path. A core component is a 'momentum' term, mimicking the cavy's ability to maintain and adjust its velocity during movement, coupled with a 'reflex' mechanism that allows for rapid directional changes. We demonstrate the efficacy of AC through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and dynamic adjustment capabilities are key to its performance. Finally, we discuss the potential extensions and future research directions for AC, including incorporating environmental constraints and adaptive parameter tuning.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Algorithm Fault Tolerance Mechanism
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to fault tolerance in distributed quantum algorithms, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed algorithms reliant on classical communication face insurmountable limitations within the context of quantum computing. This research proposes a mechanism where nodes within a quantum network communicate and synchronize through entangled states, enabling the detection and correction of node failures without the need for classical relaying. The core of this mechanism involves carefully manipulating and measuring entangled states to ensure the integrity of computations. We outline a theoretical framework for constructing such a system and demonstrate its potential to significantly enhance the reliability of large-scale quantum computing tasks. The key contributions of this work lie in exploring a fundamentally different paradigm for distributed quantum computation, one that directly harnesses the power of quantum entanglement to achieve robust fault tolerance. This approach represents a crucial step towards realizing scalable and dependable quantum distributed computing architectures.

abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with profound implications for quantum computing and communication. The core mechanism leverages a continuous, iterative adjustment of the entangled state's geometry, providing a robust and adaptable simulation framework. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in generating entangled states with intricate topologies.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Parameter Optimization Framework
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, particularly machine learning. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex landscapes and computationally intensive tasks. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning parameter optimization framework leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum neural network parameters, offering a significant improvement in learning efficiency and model accuracy. We propose a framework that utilizes quantum properties to reduce computational complexity and enhance the exploration of the parameter space. The core mechanism centers around harnessing quantum entanglement to facilitate rapid and nuanced parameter adjustments, ultimately leading to superior model performance. The paper details the design of this framework, outlines the theoretical underpinnings, and presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Estimation of Online Fan Perception Scores for Korean Professional Baseball Managers Using Machine Learning-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: 이 연구의 목적은 소셜 빅데이터와 머신러닝 기반 감성분석을 활용하여 한국프로야구 감독에 대한 온라인 팬 인식을 분석하고, 감독별 긍정·부정 인식점수를 산출하는 것이다. 이 연구의 목적을 달성하기 위해서 동영상 플랫폼 유튜브에서 2025년 3월 22일을 기준으로 한 달간 한국프로야구 하이라이트 영상에 달린 총 53,718건의 댓글을 수집하였다. 자료수집은 유튜브 API를 활용하여 Python 3 기반 웹 크롤링 자동화 프로그램을 사용하였다. 수집된 자료 중 감독과 관련된 2,154건의 댓글을 최종 분석 대상으로 선별하였으며, 댓글 자료를 토큰화한 후 명사, 동사, 형용사만 추출하였다. 추출한 단어 중 공통어, 불용어를 전처리한 후 BOW(Bag of Words) 방법을 활용하여 텍스트 데이터를 정형화하였다. 이후 LASSO(Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator)를 적용하여 주요 감성어를 선별하고, 로지스틱 회귀모형으로 댓글별 긍정·부정 감성확률을 예측하여 감독별 온라인 팬 인식점수를 산출하였다. 분석 결과, 한국프로야구 감독의 긍정점수는 26.2점으로 나타났으며, 부정점수는 73.8점으로 나타났다. 10개 구단 중 LG 트윈스 감독이 긍정점수 55.0점, 부정점수 45.0점으로 가장 높은 점수를 받았으며, KIA 타이거즈 감독이 긍정점수 14.6점, 부정점수 85.4점으로 가장 낮은 점수를 받았다. 결론적으로 이 연구는 소셜미디어 댓글 분석을 통해 한국프로야구 감독에 대한 온라인 팬 인식의 형성 양상을 보여주었으며, 감독 관련 팬 인식을 정량적으로 파악할 수 있는 기초자료로 활용될 것이다.

title: AI for prognostic assessment of diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma using H&E whole‐slide images
abstract: Abstract Prediction of the outcome of large B‐cell lymphomas/high‐grade B‐cell lymphomas (DLBCLs/HGBCLs) is based on clinical parameters and molecular testing, for example, for rearrangements of MYC (MYC‐R) and MYC‐R in combination with BCL2 and BCL6 translocations (double/triple hit). However, the group of DLBCL/HGBCL with poor outcome is not confined to MYC‐R lymphomas, and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing for MYC‐R misses several high‐risk lymphomas. We aimed to understand if artificial intelligence (AI) trained to identify MYC‐R will delineate a poor prognostic subgroup. We generated a collection of digital hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained slides of DLBCL/HGBCL ( N = 2018) annotated for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 translocations. A multiple‐instance deep learning AI model for the identification of MYC‐R alone or as double/triple hit was established using 1035 H&E‐stained slides and evaluated on an external test cohort ( N = 499). A pretrained tumor tissue classifier improved reliability and interpretability by focusing the model on tumor areas. Our model score reflects a morphological “MYCness” in DLBCL/HGBCL and demonstrates a strong association with overall survival (OS) and progression‐free survival (PFS) in the external test cohort. This was confirmed with an additional clinical test cohort ( N = 484) without FISH labels. The AI model scores correlate with various molecular features of DLBCL/HGBCL, including BCL2 and MYC gene expression, and the high‐grade gene expression signature, but also features of the tumor microenvironment. Multivariate analysis, adjusted for International Prognostic Index (IPI) factors, demonstrated the prognostic significance of our model in identifying high‐risk cases for both PFS and OS.

title: Generalized Bayesian Clustering with Regression for Unaligned Longitudinal Binary Data
abstract: We propose a generalized Bayesian clustering with regression model for unaligned longitudinal binary outcomes, motivated by seizure diary data from the Human Epilepsy Project. Seizure diaries are sparse, irregularly observed, and vary enormously across patients. A single fully-specified generative model tends to be either misspecified or computationally inefficient. We address the challenge by two strategies. We set up a regression by way of clustering as model-based clustering using a mixture model. For the latter, we take a generalized Bayesian perspective which replaces the full likelihood with a loss-based update using a generalized likelihood. We combine a trajectory similarity loss and a regression loss, so that clustering is informed by both trajectory similarity and the prediction of outcomes The trajectory similarity loss is constructed by representing each trajectory as an (empirical) distribution of subsequences, called reads, and then is defined based on the sliced Wasserstein distance between these empirical distributions. This loss allows alignment-free comparison of sequences that are irregularly observed or temporally misaligned, and it scales quasi-linearly in trajectory length. The regression loss is the negative log-likelihood of a probit regression. A prior on the cluster-specific parameters is defined by way of a Dirichlet process prior on the mixing measure.

title: Rock, Paper, Scissors, ... Dynamite - A Model of Disruption from New Technologies
abstract: We seek to understand the effect of adding disruptive highly-capable new technologies to competitions by assessing the addition of Dynamite to Rock-Paper-Scissors. We find that providing a versatile Dynamite move to only one player provides limited value (win probability increases from 50% to 55.5%) and is played rarely. That value decreases further if the game is expanded beyond just the original three moves. We also observe several mechanisms by which prior moves can become strategically unplayable, or obsolete. We hope that this model illustrates some non-intuitive aspects of developing new versatile technologies. We also hope that it illustrates some pitfalls for developers and integrators to avoid in order to create value rather than merely capability.

title: Resource supply dynamics control stability and chaos in complex ecosystems
abstract: Ecological interactions are often mediated by feedbacks between organisms and their resource environments. Yet, how resource supply dynamics dictate collective dynamical phases of an ecosystem remains unclear. Here, we analyse a generalised consumer--resource model with non-reciprocal interactions to demonstrate that self-renewing versus externally-supplied resources yield fundamentally different dynamical phase diagrams. As interactions become increasingly non-reciprocal, ecosystems relying on self-renewing resources transition from stable dynamics to chaos and ultimately to infeasibility. By contrast, ecosystems with externally-supplied resources remain stable over a broader parameter range and transition to infeasibility without experiencing an intervening chaotic phase. Using the cavity method, we derive a unified stability condition applicable to a broad class of resource supply functions, explaining why externally-supplied resources can expand the stable region. We show that stability hinges crucially on the susceptibility of resources to perturbations, which depends strongly on their supply. Further, we show that external resource supply suppresses chaos in the unstable region by drastically reducing the susceptibility of resources closest to extinction. Our findings demonstrate that resource dynamics fundamentally reshape the accessible dynamical behaviours of an ecosystem, with implications for interpreting microbial community experiments.

title: Likelihood-Constrained Acoustic Reranking for Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation in LLM-Based ASR
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems achieve strong performance on conventional speech data by leveraging powerful linguistic priors and multilingual capabilities. However, under challenging conditions, these priors can override acoustic evidence, resulting in unintended translation, instruction execution, repetition, or catastrophic deletion. We propose Likelihood-Constrained Acoustic Reranking (LCAR), a training-free decoding method that improves acoustic grounding while preserving support from the base model. At each decoding step, LCAR first retains tokens whose base-model likelihood falls within a margin of the greedy token, then reranks them using an acoustic compatibility score computed from attention-pooled audio embeddings and the existing LM head. By restricting acoustic intervention to plausible, model-supported alternatives, LCAR requires no additional training, external detector, reference transcript, or auxiliary model at inference. We evaluate LCAR on four LLM-based ASR systems using human-audited TTS and open-source speech challenge suites. At $δ=0.60$, LCAR removes 38.8--57.1\% of detector-identified hallucination failures while largely maintaining WER/CER on standard open-source test sets.

title: Two Centuries of Sexism in British Parliament: A Computational Analysis of Women's Representation in the Hansard Corpus
abstract: The language a legislature uses to debate women's rights, even in favour of them, encodes systematic patterns of sexism that persist across two centuries. In this work, we analyse 6,531 speeches over 200 years of UK parliamentary debate (Hansard, 1803-2005) by using large language models to classify a speaker's perspective towards women's suffrage and political representation, as well as analyse sexist speech in parliament from the lens of the Ambivalent Sexism Inventory. We also release this parliamentary dataset, an organized and metadata-enriched version of the publicly available Hansard Corpus optimized for computational social science research, with 6.7 million speeches across 1.2 million debates, with 89% gender-matching for speeches by MPs from the House of Commons. We find that 54% of speeches opposing women's representation contain sexist content, compared to 21% of speeches that are for the cause, and that the two sides use fundamentally different types of sexism: anti-suffrage rhetoric combines hostile and benevolent framing, while pro-suffrage sexism is overwhelmingly benevolent. Female MPs support women's political rights at 93% compared to 70% for male MPs, a gap that closes only after enfranchisement. Our findings are evidence that benevolent and hostile sexism are used in different rhetorical contexts in a manner consistent with the theory of Ambivalent Sexism.

title: Optimization benchmark results for role-based diversity-enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization algorithms
abstract: This dataset contains benchmark results of selected optimization algorithms evaluated on 32 continuous optimization problems with dimensionalities of 100, 500, and 1000 variables. The dataset includes full convergence histories and aggregated performance summaries for multiple PSO variants and baseline optimization algorithms.

title: Enhancing AI Dialogue through Dual Role Assignment: An Investigation of User-AI Professional Role Sharing
abstract: Conversational AI systems increasingly employ role/persona prompting to elicit domain-specific responses, yet roles are typically assigned only to the AI side while the user remains a neutral questioner. This study empirically investigates how dialogue content transforms when professional roles are assigned not only to the AI but also to the user, and when both parties share the same role. We conducted controlled dialogues about an identical line-drawing stimulus under four role-assignment conditions (no-role, AI-only role, user-only role, and both roles) across five professional roles (detective, psychologist, artist, architect, natural scientist) and four contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, OpenAI o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro), yielding 64 sessions and 320 question–response pairs. Quantitative term-frequency analysis of the detective role—presented as a representative case with the clearest lexical shifts—revealed that the shared-role condition increased domain-specific terminology compared to baseline and single-role conditions, a pattern also observed in the other four roles. Qualitative close readings of the detective role suggested that shared roles were associated with stronger expertise-oriented reasoning, multiperspectivity, and characteristics resembling professional peer exchange. Notably, user-side role assignment alone altered model responses even without an explicit AI role instruction. evidence.title: Enhancing AI Dialogue through Dual Role Assignment: An Investigation of User-AI Professional Role Sharing
evidence.abstract: Conversational AI systems increasingly employ role/persona prompting to elicit domain-specific responses, yet roles are typically assigned only to the AI side while the user remains a neutral questioner. This study empirically investigates how dialogue content transforms when professional roles are assigned not only to the AI but also to the user, and when both parties share the same role. We conducted controlled dialogues about an identical line-drawing stimulus under four role-assignment conditions (no-role, AI-only role, user-only role, and both roles) across five professional roles (detective, psychologist, artist, architect, natural scientist) and four contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, OpenAI o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro), yielding 64 sessions and 320 question–response pairs. Quantitative term-frequency analysis of the detective role—presented as a representative case with the clearest lexical shifts—revealed that the shared-role condition increased domain-specific terminology compared to baseline and single-role conditions, a pattern also observed in the other four roles.
